07 — DSA + Machine Coding for Senior FE (2026)

Patterns · Worked problems · 10 machine-coding components · Daily drills

Merged from v1/04 (DSA + FE coding) and v3/10 (machine coding section). FE-focused DSA — what FAANG actually asks senior FE candidates, not pure CP.

How senior FE DSA differs from CP: FAANG FE loops ask medium-difficulty DSA (rarely hard graph/DP), but score *communication*, *clean idiomatic JS*, *edge-case rigor*, and *complexity articulation*. Machine-coding rounds are the real differentiator at senior — a11y, state modeling, cleanup, and "what would you do with 30 more minutes" talking points. Optimize prep accordingly: ~60% machine coding, ~40% DSA.

Part 1 — FAANG-relevant DSA patterns

1.1 Pattern cheat sheet

PatternWhenTypical problems
Two pointersSorted array / linked list, find pair / tripletTwo-sum sorted, container with most water
Sliding windowSubarray / substring with constraintLongest substring without repeat, min window
Fast / slow pointerLinked list cycle / middleFloyd's cycle, palindrome list
Hash map / setLookup in O(1)Two-sum, group anagrams, longest consecutive
Stack / monotonic stackNext greater / smaller, bracketsDaily temperatures, valid parens, largest rect
Queue / dequeBFS, sliding-window maxLevel-order, sliding max
BFSShortest path on unweighted graphWord ladder, rotting oranges
DFS / backtrackingAll paths / permutations / subsetsPermutations, N-queens, sudoku
Dynamic programmingOptimal substructure + overlapping subproblemsClimbing stairs, longest common subseq, knapsack
GreedyLocal optimum yields global optimumActivity selection, jump game
Heap / priority queueTop-K, k-way mergeKth largest, merge K sorted lists
TriePrefix lookups, autocompleteWord search, autocomplete
Union-FindConnected components, MSTNumber of islands II, accounts merge
Bit manipulationSets fit in 32 bits; XOR tricksSingle number, sum of two without +

Pattern recognition decision tree

  • "Subarray/substring + constraint (sum/distinct/k)" → sliding window.
  • "Sorted input + find pair/triplet/partition" → two pointers.
  • "Top/smallest K, or merge K streams" → heap.
  • "Next greater/smaller, span, histogram" → monotonic stack.
  • "Shortest path, unweighted, level count" → BFS.
  • "All combinations/permutations/partitions" → backtracking.
  • "Count ways / min cost with overlapping subproblems" → DP (start recursive + memo, then tabulate).
  • "Dynamic connectivity / grouping" → union-find.
  • "Prefix/dictionary matching" → trie.

Sliding window — template

When to use: contiguous subarray/substring optimizing a constraint (longest/shortest/count) that is *monotonic* as the window grows. Complexity: O(n) time, O(k) space for the window map.

// Generic variable-size window: longest window satisfying isValid()
function longestWindow(arr, expand, shrink, isValid, state) {
  let left = 0, best = 0;
  for (let right = 0; right < arr.length; right++) {
    expand(state, arr[right]);
    while (!isValid(state)) { shrink(state, arr[left]); left++; }
    best = Math.max(best, right - left + 1);
  }
  return best;
}

Representative problem — Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters:

function lengthOfLongestSubstring(s) {
  const last = new Map(); // char -> last seen index
  let left = 0, best = 0;
  for (let right = 0; right < s.length; right++) {
    const c = s[right];
    if (last.has(c) && last.get(c) >= left) left = last.get(c) + 1;
    last.set(c, right);
    best = Math.max(best, right - left + 1);
  }
  return best; // O(n) time, O(min(n, charset)) space
}

Representative problem — Minimum Window Substring (shrinking window with need-counts):

function minWindow(s, t) {
  const need = new Map();
  for (const c of t) need.set(c, (need.get(c) ?? 0) + 1);
  let required = need.size, formed = 0, left = 0;
  let res = [Infinity, 0, 0];
  const win = new Map();
  for (let right = 0; right < s.length; right++) {
    const c = s[right];
    win.set(c, (win.get(c) ?? 0) + 1);
    if (need.has(c) && win.get(c) === need.get(c)) formed++;
    while (formed === required) {
      if (right - left + 1 < res[0]) res = [right - left + 1, left, right];
      const lc = s[left++];
      win.set(lc, win.get(lc) - 1);
      if (need.has(lc) && win.get(lc) < need.get(lc)) formed--;
    }
  }
  return res[0] === Infinity ? "" : s.slice(res[1], res[2] + 1); // O(n)
}

Two pointers — template

When to use: sorted array/linked list, or converging from both ends; partition problems; in-place dedupe. Complexity: O(n) after an O(n log n) sort if needed.

function twoSumSorted(nums, target) {
  let lo = 0, hi = nums.length - 1;
  while (lo < hi) {
    const sum = nums[lo] + nums[hi];
    if (sum === target) return [lo, hi];
    sum < target ? lo++ : hi--;
  }
  return [-1, -1]; // O(n) time, O(1) space
}

Representative problem — 3Sum (sort + fix one + two-pointer, dedupe both layers):

function threeSum(nums) {
  nums.sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const res = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < nums.length - 2; i++) {
    if (i > 0 && nums[i] === nums[i - 1]) continue; // skip dup anchor
    let lo = i + 1, hi = nums.length - 1;
    while (lo < hi) {
      const sum = nums[i] + nums[lo] + nums[hi];
      if (sum < 0) lo++;
      else if (sum > 0) hi--;
      else {
        res.push([nums[i], nums[lo], nums[hi]]);
        while (lo < hi && nums[lo] === nums[lo + 1]) lo++;
        while (lo < hi && nums[hi] === nums[hi - 1]) hi--;
        lo++; hi--;
      }
    }
  }
  return res; // O(n^2) time, O(1) extra (excluding output)
}

Fast / slow pointer — template

When to use: cycle detection, middle of list, nth-from-end without length. Complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space.

function hasCycle(head) {
  let slow = head, fast = head;
  while (fast && fast.next) {
    slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next;
    if (slow === fast) return true;
  }
  return false;
}
// Find cycle start (Floyd): after meeting, reset one pointer to head, advance both by 1.
function detectCycleStart(head) {
  let slow = head, fast = head;
  while (fast && fast.next) {
    slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next;
    if (slow === fast) {
      let p = head;
      while (p !== slow) { p = p.next; slow = slow.next; }
      return p;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

Monotonic stack — template

When to use: next greater/smaller element, stock span, histogram area, trapping rain water. Complexity: O(n) — each index pushed/popped once.

function dailyTemperatures(temps) {
  const res = new Array(temps.length).fill(0);
  const stack = []; // indices, decreasing temperature
  for (let i = 0; i < temps.length; i++) {
    while (stack.length && temps[i] > temps[stack.at(-1)]) {
      const j = stack.pop();
      res[j] = i - j;
    }
    stack.push(i);
  }
  return res; // O(n) time, O(n) space
}

Representative — Largest Rectangle in Histogram (sentinel-terminated monotonic stack):

function largestRectangleArea(h) {
  const stack = [], heights = [...h, 0];
  let best = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < heights.length; i++) {
    while (stack.length && heights[i] < heights[stack.at(-1)]) {
      const height = heights[stack.pop()];
      const width = stack.length ? i - stack.at(-1) - 1 : i;
      best = Math.max(best, height * width);
    }
    stack.push(i);
  }
  return best; // O(n)
}

BFS — template

When to use: shortest path / fewest steps on unweighted graph or grid; level-order. Use a frontier array with a fresh array per level (Array.shift is O(n) — avoid as a queue). Complexity: O(V + E).

function bfs(start, neighbors, keyOf) {
  const seen = new Set([keyOf(start)]);
  let frontier = [start], steps = 0;
  while (frontier.length) {
    const next = [];
    for (const node of frontier) {
      for (const nb of neighbors(node)) {
        const k = keyOf(nb);
        if (!seen.has(k)) { seen.add(k); next.push(nb); }
      }
    }
    frontier = next; steps++;
  }
  return steps;
}

Representative — Rotting Oranges (multi-source BFS, count minutes):

function orangesRotting(grid) {
  const R = grid.length, C = grid[0].length;
  let frontier = [], fresh = 0;
  for (let r = 0; r < R; r++) for (let c = 0; c < C; c++) {
    if (grid[r][c] === 2) frontier.push([r, c]);
    else if (grid[r][c] === 1) fresh++;
  }
  let minutes = 0;
  const dirs = [[1,0],[-1,0],[0,1],[0,-1]];
  while (frontier.length && fresh) {
    const next = [];
    for (const [r, c] of frontier) {
      for (const [dr, dc] of dirs) {
        const nr = r + dr, nc = c + dc;
        if (nr >= 0 && nr < R && nc >= 0 && nc < C && grid[nr][nc] === 1) {
          grid[nr][nc] = 2; fresh--; next.push([nr, nc]);
        }
      }
    }
    frontier = next; minutes++;
  }
  return fresh ? -1 : minutes; // O(R*C)
}

DFS / backtracking — template

When to use: enumerate all subsets/permutations/partitions; constraint satisfaction (N-queens, sudoku). Complexity: exponential by nature; prune aggressively.

function backtrack(choices, isComplete, isValid) {
  const res = [], path = [];
  (function dfs(start) {
    if (isComplete(path)) { res.push([...path]); return; }
    for (let i = start; i < choices.length; i++) {
      if (!isValid(path, choices[i])) continue; // prune
      path.push(choices[i]);
      dfs(i + 1);          // i for combinations w/ reuse, i+1 without
      path.pop();          // undo (this is the "back" in backtracking)
    }
  })(0);
  return res;
}

Representative — Subsets and Permutations:

function subsets(nums) {
  const res = [], path = [];
  (function dfs(start) {
    res.push([...path]);
    for (let i = start; i < nums.length; i++) {
      path.push(nums[i]); dfs(i + 1); path.pop();
    }
  })(0);
  return res; // O(n * 2^n)
}
function permutations(nums) {
  const res = [], path = [], used = new Array(nums.length).fill(false);
  (function dfs() {
    if (path.length === nums.length) { res.push([...path]); return; }
    for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
      if (used[i]) continue;
      used[i] = true; path.push(nums[i]);
      dfs();
      path.pop(); used[i] = false;
    }
  })();
  return res; // O(n * n!)
}

Dynamic programming — template

When to use: optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems. Process: (1) define state, (2) recurrence, (3) base cases, (4) memoize → tabulate → space-optimize. Complexity: states × transition cost.

// Top-down memo
function solveMemo(input, { keyOf, isBase, baseValue, transitions, value }) {
  const memo = new Map();
  function dp(state) {
    const k = keyOf(state);
    if (memo.has(k)) return memo.get(k);
    if (isBase(state)) return baseValue(state);
    let best = -Infinity;
    for (const t of transitions(state)) best = Math.max(best, value(t) + dp(t));
    memo.set(k, best);
    return best;
  }
  return dp(input);
}

Representative — Coin Change (min coins, bottom-up):

function coinChange(coins, amount) {
  const dp = new Array(amount + 1).fill(Infinity);
  dp[0] = 0;
  for (let a = 1; a <= amount; a++) {
    for (const c of coins) {
      if (c <= a && dp[a - c] + 1 < dp[a]) dp[a] = dp[a - c] + 1;
    }
  }
  return dp[amount] === Infinity ? -1 : dp[amount]; // O(amount * coins)
}

Representative — Longest Common Subsequence (2D table, space-optimizable to 2 rows):

function lcs(a, b) {
  const m = a.length, n = b.length;
  const dp = Array.from({ length: m + 1 }, () => new Array(n + 1).fill(0));
  for (let i = 1; i <= m; i++)
    for (let j = 1; j <= n; j++)
      dp[i][j] = a[i - 1] === b[j - 1]
        ? dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1
        : Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);
  return dp[m][n]; // O(m*n) time/space
}

Heap / priority queue — template

When to use: top-K, k-way merge, streaming median, Dijkstra. JS has no built-in heap — implement a binary heap or carry this snippet. Complexity: push/pop O(log n).

class MinHeap {
  constructor(cmp = (a, b) => a - b) { this.a = []; this.cmp = cmp; }
  size() { return this.a.length; }
  peek() { return this.a[0]; }
  push(x) {
    const a = this.a; a.push(x);
    let i = a.length - 1;
    while (i > 0) {
      const p = (i - 1) >> 1;
      if (this.cmp(a[i], a[p]) >= 0) break;
      [a[i], a[p]] = [a[p], a[i]]; i = p;
    }
  }
  pop() {
    const a = this.a, top = a[0], last = a.pop();
    if (a.length) {
      a[0] = last;
      let i = 0;
      for (;;) {
        let s = i, l = 2 * i + 1, r = 2 * i + 2;
        if (l < a.length && this.cmp(a[l], a[s]) < 0) s = l;
        if (r < a.length && this.cmp(a[r], a[s]) < 0) s = r;
        if (s === i) break;
        [a[i], a[s]] = [a[s], a[i]]; i = s;
      }
    }
    return top;
  }
}

Representative — Kth Largest (min-heap of size k) and Merge K Sorted Lists:

function findKthLargest(nums, k) {
  const heap = new MinHeap();
  for (const x of nums) {
    heap.push(x);
    if (heap.size() > k) heap.pop();
  }
  return heap.peek(); // O(n log k)
}
function mergeKLists(lists) {
  const heap = new MinHeap((a, b) => a.val - b.val);
  for (const node of lists) if (node) heap.push(node);
  const dummy = { next: null }; let tail = dummy;
  while (heap.size()) {
    const node = heap.pop();
    tail.next = node; tail = node;
    if (node.next) heap.push(node.next);
  }
  return dummy.next; // O(N log k)
}

Trie — template

When to use: prefix search, autocomplete, word-search dictionaries. Complexity: insert/search O(L).

class Trie {
  constructor() { this.root = { children: new Map(), end: false }; }
  insert(word) {
    let node = this.root;
    for (const ch of word) {
      if (!node.children.has(ch)) node.children.set(ch, { children: new Map(), end: false });
      node = node.children.get(ch);
    }
    node.end = true;
  }
  _walk(prefix) {
    let node = this.root;
    for (const ch of prefix) {
      if (!node.children.has(ch)) return null;
      node = node.children.get(ch);
    }
    return node;
  }
  search(word) { return !!this._walk(word)?.end; }
  startsWith(prefix) { return !!this._walk(prefix); }
}

Union-Find — template

When to use: dynamic connectivity, grouping, cycle detection in undirected graphs, accounts merge. Complexity: ~O(α(n)) per op with path compression + union by rank.

class DSU {
  constructor(n) { this.parent = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => i); this.rank = new Array(n).fill(0); }
  find(x) {
    while (this.parent[x] !== x) { this.parent[x] = this.parent[this.parent[x]]; x = this.parent[x]; }
    return x;
  }
  union(a, b) {
    let ra = this.find(a), rb = this.find(b);
    if (ra === rb) return false;
    if (this.rank[ra] < this.rank[rb]) [ra, rb] = [rb, ra];
    this.parent[rb] = ra;
    if (this.rank[ra] === this.rank[rb]) this.rank[ra]++;
    return true;
  }
}

Representative — Number of Connected Components:

function countComponents(n, edges) {
  const dsu = new DSU(n);
  let components = n;
  for (const [a, b] of edges) if (dsu.union(a, b)) components--;
  return components; // O(E α(n))
}

Bit manipulation — template

When to use: sets that fit in 32 bits, XOR pairing tricks, subset enumeration. Complexity: O(1) per op.

const setBit   = (n, i) => n | (1 << i);
const clearBit = (n, i) => n & ~(1 << i);
const hasBit   = (n, i) => (n >> i & 1) === 1;
const popcount = n => { let c = 0; while (n) { n &= n - 1; c++; } return c; };

// Single Number: XOR cancels pairs, leaving the unique value. O(n), O(1).
const singleNumber = nums => nums.reduce((acc, x) => acc ^ x, 0);

1.2 Big-O cheat sheet

OpArrayLinked ListHashBST balanced
Access by indexO(1)O(n)—O(log n)
Search by valueO(n)O(n)O(1) avgO(log n)
Insert at endO(1)O(1)O(1) avgO(log n)
Insert at middleO(n)O(1) given nodeO(1) avgO(log n)
DeleteO(n)O(1) given nodeO(1) avgO(log n)

JS-specific complexity gotchas (interviewers probe these)

  • Array.prototype.shift/unshift are O(n) — never use them as a queue in a hot loop; use an index pointer or a frontier array.
  • Array.prototype.includes/indexOf are O(n) — prefer Set.has/Map.has for membership.
  • Spreading [...arr] and arr.slice() are O(n) — watch for accidental O(n²) when done inside a loop.
  • Object key lookup is amortized O(1) but insertion-order + string coercion of keys differs from Map; Map preserves insertion order and accepts any key type — prefer it for caches/LRU.
  • Array.sort is O(n log n) and spec-stable since ES2019 (safe in 2026). It sorts lexicographically by default — always pass a comparator for numbers.
  • Recursion depth: V8 stack ~10–15k frames. Deep recursion on linked lists / DFS on large graphs can RangeError; convert to an explicit stack.
  • Math.max(...bigArray) can blow the argument-count limit (~65k–500k) — use a reduce.

The 6 highest-frequency ones, solved

// 1) Two Sum — hash complement. O(n)/O(n).
function twoSum(nums, target) {
  const seen = new Map();
  for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
    if (seen.has(target - nums[i])) return [seen.get(target - nums[i]), i];
    seen.set(nums[i], i);
  }
  return [];
}

// 2) Maximum Subarray — Kadane's. O(n)/O(1).
function maxSubArray(nums) {
  let cur = nums[0], best = nums[0];
  for (let i = 1; i < nums.length; i++) {
    cur = Math.max(nums[i], cur + nums[i]);
    best = Math.max(best, cur);
  }
  return best;
}

// 3) Valid Parentheses — stack. O(n)/O(n).
function isValid(s) {
  const pairs = { ")": "(", "]": "[", "}": "{" }, st = [];
  for (const ch of s) {
    if (ch in pairs) { if (st.pop() !== pairs[ch]) return false; }
    else st.push(ch);
  }
  return st.length === 0;
}

// 4) Reverse Linked List — iterative. O(n)/O(1).
function reverseList(head) {
  let prev = null;
  while (head) { const next = head.next; head.next = prev; prev = head; head = next; }
  return prev;
}

// 5) Binary Tree Level Order — BFS. O(n).
function levelOrder(root) {
  if (!root) return [];
  const res = []; let frontier = [root];
  while (frontier.length) {
    const next = [], row = [];
    for (const node of frontier) {
      row.push(node.val);
      if (node.left) next.push(node.left);
      if (node.right) next.push(node.right);
    }
    res.push(row); frontier = next;
  }
  return res;
}

// 6) Search in Rotated Sorted Array — modified binary search. O(log n).
function searchRotated(nums, target) {
  let lo = 0, hi = nums.length - 1;
  while (lo <= hi) {
    const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1;
    if (nums[mid] === target) return mid;
    if (nums[lo] <= nums[mid]) { // left half sorted
      if (nums[lo] <= target && target < nums[mid]) hi = mid - 1; else lo = mid + 1;
    } else {                     // right half sorted
      if (nums[mid] < target && target <= nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;
    }
  }
  return -1;
}

// Promise pool — bounded concurrency, preserves result order, tasks are () => Promise.
async function promisePool(tasks, limit) {
  const results = new Array(tasks.length);
  let i = 0;
  async function worker() {
    while (i < tasks.length) {
      const idx = i++;
      results[idx] = await tasks[idx]();
    }
  }
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, tasks.length) }, worker));
  return results;
}

// timeout(promise, ms) — rejects if the wrapped promise doesn't settle in time.
function timeout(promise, ms) {
  let id;
  const t = new Promise((_, reject) => {
    id = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`Timed out after ${ms}ms`)), ms);
  });
  return Promise.race([promise, t]).finally(() => clearTimeout(id));
}

// retry with exponential backoff + jitter.
async function retry(fn, { attempts = 3, base = 200, factor = 2 } = {}) {
  let lastErr;
  for (let n = 0; n < attempts; n++) {
    try { return await fn(); }
    catch (err) {
      lastErr = err;
      if (n === attempts - 1) break;
      const delay = base * factor ** n * (0.5 + Math.random()); // jitter
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
  throw lastErr;
}

// deepClone with cycle handling (use structuredClone in prod; this shows the algorithm).
function deepClone(value, seen = new WeakMap()) {
  if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") return value;
  if (seen.has(value)) return seen.get(value); // break cycles
  if (value instanceof Date) return new Date(value);
  if (value instanceof RegExp) return new RegExp(value.source, value.flags);
  if (value instanceof Map) {
    const out = new Map(); seen.set(value, out);
    for (const [k, v] of value) out.set(deepClone(k, seen), deepClone(v, seen));
    return out;
  }
  if (value instanceof Set) {
    const out = new Set(); seen.set(value, out);
    for (const v of value) out.add(deepClone(v, seen));
    return out;
  }
  const out = Array.isArray(value) ? [] : {};
  seen.set(value, out);
  for (const k of Reflect.ownKeys(value)) out[k] = deepClone(value[k], seen);
  return out;
}

// LRU cache using Map insertion order (delete+set moves key to "most recent").
class LRUCache {
  constructor(capacity) { this.cap = capacity; this.map = new Map(); }
  get(key) {
    if (!this.map.has(key)) return undefined;
    const v = this.map.get(key);
    this.map.delete(key); this.map.set(key, v); // refresh recency
    return v;
  }
  put(key, value) {
    if (this.map.has(key)) this.map.delete(key);
    else if (this.map.size >= this.cap) this.map.delete(this.map.keys().next().value); // evict LRU
    this.map.set(key, value);
  }
}

2.1 Image carousel with autoplay

function Carousel({ images, autoPlayMs = 4000 }) {
  const [i, setI] = useState(0);
  const n = images.length;
  const next = useCallback(() => setI(p => (p + 1) % n), [n]);
  const prev = useCallback(() => setI(p => (p - 1 + n) % n), [n]);

    window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);

      <button onClick={next} aria-label="Next">›</button>
      <span aria-live="polite" className="sr-only">Slide {i+1} of {n}</span>

import { useState, useRef, useCallback, useEffect, useId } from "react";

function useReducedMotion() {
  const [reduced, setReduced] = useState(
    () => window.matchMedia?.("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches ?? false
  );
  useEffect(() => {
    const mq = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)");
    const on = e => setReduced(e.matches);
    mq.addEventListener("change", on);
    return () => mq.removeEventListener("change", on);

export function Carousel({ images, autoPlayMs = 4000 }) {
  const n = images.length;
  const [i, setI] = useState(0);
  const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false);
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const groupId = useId();
  const touchX = useRef(null);

  const go = useCallback(delta => setI(p => (p + delta + n) % n), [n]);
  const next = useCallback(() => go(1), [go]);
  const prev = useCallback(() => go(-1), [go]);

  // Autoplay: paused on hover/focus and when reduced-motion is requested.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!autoPlayMs || paused || reduced || n <= 1) return;
    const id = setInterval(next, autoPlayMs);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, [autoPlayMs, paused, reduced, n, next]);

  const onKeyDown = useCallback(e => {
    if (e.key === "ArrowRight") { e.preventDefault(); next(); }
    else if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") { e.preventDefault(); prev(); }
  }, [next, prev]);

  const onTouchStart = e => { touchX.current = e.touches[0].clientX; };
  const onTouchEnd = e => {
    if (touchX.current == null) return;
    const dx = e.changedTouches[0].clientX - touchX.current;
    if (Math.abs(dx) > 40) (dx < 0 ? next : prev)();
    touchX.current = null;
  };

  if (n === 0) return <div role="region" aria-label="Carousel">No images</div>;

  return (
    <div
      role="region"
      aria-roledescription="carousel"
      aria-label="Image carousel"
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      onMouseEnter={() => setPaused(true)}
      onMouseLeave={() => setPaused(false)}
      onFocusCapture={() => setPaused(true)}
      onBlurCapture={() => setPaused(false)}
      onTouchStart={onTouchStart}
      onTouchEnd={onTouchEnd}
    >
      <div aria-live={paused ? "polite" : "off"}>
        {images.map((img, idx) => (
          <div
            key={img.src}
            id={`${groupId}-slide-${idx}`}
            role="group"
            aria-roledescription="slide"
            aria-label={`${idx + 1} of ${n}`}
            hidden={idx !== i}
          >
            <img
              src={img.src}
              alt={img.alt}
              loading={Math.abs(idx - i) <= 1 ? "eager" : "lazy"}
              decoding="async"
              draggable={false}
            />
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>

      <button type="button" onClick={prev} aria-label="Previous slide">‹</button>
      <button type="button" onClick={next} aria-label="Next slide">›</button>

      <div role="tablist" aria-label="Choose slide">
        {images.map((_, idx) => (
          <button
            key={idx}

            role="tab"

  • Autoplay lifecycle: setInterval recreated on dependency change; cleared on unmount and when paused/reduced. Mention that for drift-free timing you'd use a recursive setTimeout and that background tabs throttle timers — pause via the Page Visibility API (visibilitychange).

  • "30 more minutes": virtualize for hundreds of slides, preload next image, deep-linkable index via URL, infinite loop with cloned edge slides.

Complete implementation with loading/error/end states

import { useState, useRef, useEffect, useCallback } from "react";

// Sentinel-based infinite scroll. Guards against duplicate loads and unmount races.
function useInfiniteScroll({ hasMore, loading, onLoadMore, rootMargin = "400px" }) {
  const sentinelRef = useRef(null);
  // Keep latest values in a ref so the observer callback never goes stale
  // without re-creating the observer on every render.
  const state = useRef({ hasMore, loading, onLoadMore });
  state.current = { hasMore, loading, onLoadMore };

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = sentinelRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const io = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
      const { hasMore, loading, onLoadMore } = state.current;
      if (entries[0].isIntersecting && hasMore && !loading) onLoadMore();
    }, { rootMargin });
    io.observe(el);
    return () => io.disconnect();
  }, [rootMargin]);

  return sentinelRef;
}

export function Feed({ fetchPage }) {
  const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
  const [page, setPage] = useState(0);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState(null);
  const [hasMore, setHasMore] = useState(true);
  const aborter = useRef(null);

  const loadMore = useCallback(async () => {
    setLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    aborter.current?.abort();
    const ctrl = new AbortController();
    aborter.current = ctrl;
    try {
      const { data, nextHasMore } = await fetchPage(page, ctrl.signal);
      setItems(prev => [...prev, ...data]);
      setHasMore(nextHasMore);
      setPage(p => p + 1);
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.name !== "AbortError") setError(err);
    } finally {
      if (aborter.current === ctrl) setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [page, fetchPage]);

  const sentinelRef = useInfiniteScroll({ hasMore, loading, onLoadMore: loadMore });
  useEffect(() => () => aborter.current?.abort(), []); // cleanup on unmount

  return (
    <div>
      <ul aria-busy={loading}>
        {items.map(item => <li key={item.id}>{item.title}</li>)}
      </ul>

      {error && (
        <div role="alert">
          Failed to load. <button onClick={loadMore}>Retry</button>
        </div>
      )}
      {loading && <p role="status">Loading more…</p>}
      {!hasMore && !loading && <p>You've reached the end.</p>}

      {/* Observed sentinel — invisible, sits below the last item. */}
      <div ref={sentinelRef} aria-hidden="true" style={{ height: 1 }} />
    </div>
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • Why IntersectionObserver over scroll listeners: scroll fires constantly and forces layout reads; IO is off-main-thread, batched, and gives rootMargin prefetch for free. No debounce needed.
  • Duplicate-load guard: hasMore && !loading check; AbortController cancels the previous in-flight request so a fast scroller doesn't stack pages out of order.
  • Stale-closure fix: observer reads from a ref so it isn't recreated each render but always sees fresh loading/hasMore.
  • States: loading, error+retry, end-of-list, aria-busy/role="status"/role="alert".
  • Cleanup: io.disconnect() and abort in-flight fetch on unmount.
  • "30 more minutes": combine with windowing/virtualization (a 50k-item DOM kills scroll perf), cursor-based pagination over offset, scroll-position restoration on back-nav, optimistic skeletons.

Complete implementation with full focus trap

import { useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from "react";
import { createPortal } from "react-dom";

const FOCUSABLE = [
  "a[href]", "button:not([disabled])", "textarea:not([disabled])",
  "input:not([disabled])", "select:not([disabled])", '[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])',
].join(",");

export function Modal({ open, onClose, children, label, initialFocusRef }) {
  const dialogRef = useRef(null);
  const restoreRef = useRef(null);

  const getFocusable = () =>
    Array.from(dialogRef.current?.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE) ?? [])
      .filter(el => el.offsetParent !== null); // visible only

  const onKeyDown = useCallback(e => {
    if (e.key === "Escape") { e.stopPropagation(); onClose(); return; }
    if (e.key !== "Tab") return;
    const items = getFocusable();
    if (items.length === 0) { e.preventDefault(); return; }
    const first = items[0], last = items[items.length - 1];
    const active = document.activeElement;
    if (e.shiftKey && active === first) { e.preventDefault(); last.focus(); }
    else if (!e.shiftKey && active === last) { e.preventDefault(); first.focus(); }
  }, [onClose]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!open) return;
    restoreRef.current = document.activeElement; // remember opener
    const prevOverflow = document.body.style.overflow;
    document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"; // prevent background scroll

    // Defer focus until portal content is mounted/painted.
    const id = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      (initialFocusRef?.current ?? getFocusable()[0] ?? dialogRef.current)?.focus();
    });

    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(id);
      document.body.style.overflow = prevOverflow;
      restoreRef.current?.focus?.(); // return focus to opener
    };
  }, [open, initialFocusRef]);

  if (!open) return null;

  return createPortal(
    <div
      className="overlay"
      onMouseDown={e => { if (e.target === e.currentTarget) onClose(); }} // click-outside
    >
      <div
        ref={dialogRef}
        role="dialog"
        aria-modal="true"
        aria-label={label}
        tabIndex={-1}
        onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      >
        {children}
      </div>
    </div>,
    document.body
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • Portal rationale: escape overflow:hidden/z-index/transform stacking-context traps by rendering to document.body; keeps the modal visually on top regardless of where it's invoked.
  • Focus management (the 4 must-haves): (1) move focus into the dialog on open, (2) trap Tab/Shift+Tab cyclically, (3) restore focus to the trigger on close, (4) aria-modal="true" + label. Use requestAnimationFrame so focus lands after the portal paints.
  • Escape + click-outside: onMouseDown target check avoids the bug where a drag that starts inside and releases outside closes the modal.
  • Background: lock body scroll; ideally also inert/aria-hidden the rest of the app so screen readers can't navigate behind it.
  • Edge cases: no focusable children (focus the dialog), nested modals (stack with focus-trap layering), SSR (guard document).
  • "30 more minutes": native <dialog> element + showModal() for built-in trap & top-layer; animation with prefers-reduced-motion; route-driven modals; inert for older engines.

}

export function ToastProvider({ children, max = 4 }) {
  const [toasts, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, []);
  const timers = useRef(new Map()); // id -> { timeoutId, remaining, startedAt }

  const remove = useCallback(id => {
    const t = timers.current.get(id);
    if (t) { clearTimeout(t.timeoutId); timers.current.delete(id); }
    dispatch({ type: "remove", id });
  }, []);

  const schedule = useCallback((id, ms) => {
    const startedAt = Date.now();
    const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => remove(id), ms);
    timers.current.set(id, { timeoutId, remaining: ms, startedAt });
  }, [remove]);

  const addToast = useCallback((message, { type = "info", duration = 4000 } = {}) => {
    const id = ++seq;
    dispatch({ type: "add", toast: { id, message, type } });
    if (duration > 0) schedule(id, duration);
    return id;
  }, [schedule]);

  // pause/resume on hover/focus by tracking remaining time
  const pause = useCallback(id => {
    const t = timers.current.get(id);
    if (!t) return;
    clearTimeout(t.timeoutId);
    t.remaining -= Date.now() - t.startedAt;
  }, []);
  const resume = useCallback(id => {
    const t = timers.current.get(id);
    if (!t) return;
    schedule(id, Math.max(0, t.remaining));
  }, [schedule]);

  useEffect(() => () => { // cleanup every timer on unmount
    for (const { timeoutId } of timers.current.values()) clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    timers.current.clear();
  }, []);

  const visible = toasts.slice(-max);

  return (
    <ToastContext.Provider value={{ addToast, remove }}>
      {children}
      {createPortal(
        <div className="toast-region" role="region" aria-label="Notifications">
          {/* Polite live region: announced without interrupting. Errors use assertive. */}
          {visible.map(t => (
            <div
              key={t.id}
              role={t.type === "error" ? "alert" : "status"}
              aria-live={t.type === "error" ? "assertive" : "polite"}
              aria-atomic="true"
              className={`toast toast--${t.type}`}
              onMouseEnter={() => pause(t.id)}
              onMouseLeave={() => resume(t.id)}
              onFocus={() => pause(t.id)}
              onBlur={() => resume(t.id)}
            >
              <span>{t.message}</span>
              <button aria-label="Dismiss notification" onClick={() => remove(t.id)}>×</button>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>,
        document.body
      )}
    </ToastContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useToast() {
  const ctx = useContext(ToastContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("useToast must be used within ToastProvider");
  return ctx;
}

Senior talking points:

  • Imperative API via context: const { addToast } = useToast() returns an id so callers can dismiss programmatically (e.g., resolve a "Saving…" toast into "Saved").
  • Pause-on-hover correctness: naive clearTimeout loses elapsed time — track remaining and re-setTimeout on resume. This is the detail interviewers look for.
  • a11y: non-error toasts in a polite role="status" region; errors in assertive role="alert". aria-atomic so the whole toast re-reads. Dismiss buttons are labeled. Never auto-dismiss critical errors.
  • Stacking/cap: show the most recent max; queue/drop the rest to avoid spam.
  • Cleanup: clear all timers on unmount — leaked timers calling dispatch after unmount is a classic bug.
  • "30 more minutes": enter/leave animations with prefers-reduced-motion, swipe-to-dismiss, position variants, dedupe identical messages, promise-based toast.promise().

Complete implementation with keyboard + roving tabindex + read-only mode

import { useState, useRef, useCallback } from "react";

export function Rating({ value = 0, onChange, max = 5, readOnly = false, label = "Rating" }) {
  const [hover, setHover] = useState(null);
  const refs = useRef([]);
  const display = hover ?? value; // hover preview overrides committed value

  const focusStar = n => refs.current[n - 1]?.focus();

  const onKeyDown = useCallback(e => {
    if (readOnly) return;
    let next = value;
    switch (e.key) {
      case "ArrowRight": case "ArrowUp": next = Math.min(max, value + 1); break;
      case "ArrowLeft":  case "ArrowDown": next = Math.max(0, value - 1); break;
      case "Home": next = 1; break;
      case "End": next = max; break;
      default: return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
    onChange(next);
    if (next >= 1) focusStar(next);
  }, [value, max, onChange, readOnly]);

  if (readOnly) {
    return (
      <div role="img" aria-label={`${label}: ${value} out of ${max} stars`}>
        {Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => (
          <span key={i} aria-hidden="true">{i < value ? "★" : "☆"}</span>
        ))}
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div role="radiogroup" aria-label={label} onMouseLeave={() => setHover(null)}>
      {Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => i + 1).map(n => (
        <button
          key={n}
          type="button"
          ref={el => (refs.current[n - 1] = el)}
          role="radio"
          aria-checked={value === n}
          aria-label={`${n} star${n > 1 ? "s" : ""}`}
          // Roving tabindex: only the selected (or first) star is tabbable.
          tabIndex={value === n || (value === 0 && n === 1) ? 0 : -1}
          onClick={() => onChange(n)}
          onMouseEnter={() => setHover(n)}
          onFocus={() => setHover(n)}
          onBlur={() => setHover(null)}
          onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
        >
          <span aria-hidden="true">{display >= n ? "★" : "☆"}</span>
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • Pattern choice: radiogroup + radio is the WAI-ARIA-correct semantics (single choice from a set). Each star is a real button so it's clickable and announces "N stars, checked".
  • Roving tabindex: the group is a single Tab stop; arrows move within it. Only one star has tabIndex=0 at a time — critical for keyboard users not to Tab through 5 controls.
  • Hover vs commit: hover ?? value shows a live preview without mutating state; reset on mouseleave/blur.
  • Read-only variant: collapse to a single role="img" with an aria-label rather than 5 fake radios.
  • Edge cases: allow clearing to 0, keyboard Home/End, half-star (track fractional via pointer x-offset within the star), RTL arrow direction.
  • "30 more minutes": half-star precision, hover tooltip captions ("Good", "Excellent"), form integration with a hidden input + name.

2.6 Tic-tac-toe with bot

  • State: 9-cell array; winner via 8 winning lines.
  • Bot: minimax (depth-limited) OR random for entry-level.
  • Stretch: undo, scoreboard, accessible labels per cell.

Complete implementation with unbeatable minimax bot

import { useState, useCallback, useMemo } from "react";

const LINES = [
  [0,1,2],[3,4,5],[6,7,8],  // rows
  [0,3,6],[1,4,7],[2,5,8],  // cols
  [0,4,8],[2,4,6],          // diagonals
];

function getWinner(board) {
  for (const [a, b, c] of LINES) {
    if (board[a] && board[a] === board[b] && board[a] === board[c]) {
      return { player: board[a], line: [a, b, c] };
    }
  }
  return board.every(Boolean) ? { player: "draw", line: null } : null;
}

// Minimax: bot is "O" (maximizer), human "X" (minimizer). Returns best score.
function minimax(board, isBotTurn) {
  const result = getWinner(board);
  if (result) {
    if (result.player === "O") return 10;
    if (result.player === "X") return -10;
    return 0; // draw
  }
  const mark = isBotTurn ? "O" : "X";
  let best = isBotTurn ? -Infinity : Infinity;
  for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
    if (board[i]) continue;
    board[i] = mark;
    const score = minimax(board, !isBotTurn);
    board[i] = null;
    best = isBotTurn ? Math.max(best, score) : Math.min(best, score);
  }
  return best;
}

function bestMove(board) {
  let move = -1, bestScore = -Infinity;
  for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
    if (board[i]) continue;
    board[i] = "O";
    const score = minimax(board, false);
    board[i] = null;
    if (score > bestScore) { bestScore = score; move = i; }
  }
  return move;
}

export function TicTacToe() {
  const [board, setBoard] = useState(() => Array(9).fill(null));
  const result = useMemo(() => getWinner(board), [board]);

  const play = useCallback(idx => {
    if (board[idx] || result) return;
    const afterHuman = board.slice();
    afterHuman[idx] = "X";
    if (getWinner(afterHuman)) { setBoard(afterHuman); return; }
    const move = bestMove(afterHuman.slice()); // bot responds
    afterHuman[move] = "O";
    setBoard(afterHuman);
  }, [board, result]);

  const reset = () => setBoard(Array(9).fill(null));

  const status = !result ? "Your turn (X)"
    : result.player === "draw" ? "Draw"
    : result.player === "X" ? "You win!" : "Bot wins";

  return (
    <div>
      <p role="status" aria-live="polite">{status}</p>
      <div role="grid" aria-label="Tic-tac-toe board"
           style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(3, 1fr)" }}>
        {board.map((cell, i) => {
          const won = result?.line?.includes(i);
          return (
            <button
              key={i}
              role="gridcell"
              aria-label={`Cell ${Math.floor(i / 3) + 1},${(i % 3) + 1}: ${cell ?? "empty"}`}
              aria-disabled={!!cell || !!result}
              onClick={() => play(i)}
              style={{ background: won ? "#cfc" : undefined }}
            >
              {cell ?? " "}
            </button>
          );
        })}
      </div>
      <button onClick={reset}>New game</button>
    </div>
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • Win detection: precomputed 8 lines is clean and returns the winning line for highlighting; cleaner than ad-hoc row/col/diag math.
  • Minimax: explain the recursion — bot maximizes, human minimizes; terminal scores ±10/0; unbeatable because it explores the full game tree (tiny for 3×3). Mention depth-weighting (10 - depth) to prefer faster wins, and alpha-beta pruning as the optimization for larger games.
  • Immutability: never mutate board in state; minimax mutates a *copy* and undoes each move (backtracking) for speed.
  • a11y: role="grid"/gridcell, cells labeled by coordinate + content, aria-live status, disabled occupied/finished cells.
  • Edge cases: prevent moves after game over or on filled cells; draw detection; human winning move means bot shouldn't respond.
  • "30 more minutes": difficulty levels (random → depth-limited → full), undo/redo stack, configurable board size with a heuristic eval (minimax doesn't scale past 3×3), keyboard arrow navigation across the grid.

2.7 Tabs (WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices)

  • Container role="tablist"; headers role="tab" + aria-selected + aria-controls.
  • Panels role="tabpanel" + aria-labelledby.
  • Keyboard: Left/Right cycle, Home/End jump.
  • Roving tabindex.

Complete implementation (WAI-ARIA APG compliant)

import { useState, useRef, useId, useCallback } from "react";

export function Tabs({ tabs, defaultIndex = 0 }) {
  const [active, setActive] = useState(defaultIndex);
  const baseId = useId();
  const tabRefs = useRef([]);

  const tabId = i => `${baseId}-tab-${i}`;
  const panelId = i => `${baseId}-panel-${i}`;

  const onKeyDown = useCallback(e => {
    const last = tabs.length - 1;
    let next = null;
    switch (e.key) {
      case "ArrowRight": next = active === last ? 0 : active + 1; break;
      case "ArrowLeft":  next = active === 0 ? last : active - 1; break;
      case "Home": next = 0; break;
      case "End": next = last; break;
      default: return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
    setActive(next);
    tabRefs.current[next]?.focus(); // automatic activation pattern
  }, [active, tabs.length]);

  return (
    <div>
      <div role="tablist" aria-label="Content tabs">
        {tabs.map((tab, i) => (
          <button
            key={i}
            ref={el => (tabRefs.current[i] = el)}
            role="tab"
            id={tabId(i)}
            aria-selected={i === active}
            aria-controls={panelId(i)}
            tabIndex={i === active ? 0 : -1}
            onClick={() => setActive(i)}
            onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
          >
            {tab.label}
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      {tabs.map((tab, i) => (
        <div
          key={i}
          role="tabpanel"
          id={panelId(i)}
          aria-labelledby={tabId(i)}
          hidden={i !== active}
          tabIndex={0}
        >
          {i === active && tab.content}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • Roving tabindex: exactly one tab is tabIndex=0; arrows move focus, Tab leaves the tablist and lands on the panel. This is the single most-commonly-missed detail.
  • Activation model: *automatic* (focus = select, shown above) vs *manual* (arrow focuses, Enter/Space selects) — use manual when panels are expensive to render. Mention both.
  • ID wiring: aria-controls (tab→panel) and aria-labelledby (panel→tab) form the bidirectional link; useId avoids collisions across instances.
  • Lazy mount: {i === active && tab.content} so hidden panels don't render heavy trees; trade-off is losing internal state on switch (use CSS hidden to preserve).
  • Edge cases: wrap-around at ends, Home/End, RTL (swap arrow direction), disabled tabs (skip in arrow nav).
  • "30 more minutes": vertical orientation (aria-orientation, Up/Down), URL-synced active tab, overflow with scroll/more-menu.

2.8 Pagination

  • Render ellipses around current page (1 … 4 5 6 … 20).
  • Pages 1, current-1, current, current+1, last; gaps as "…".
  • aria-current="page" on the active number.

Complete implementation with robust page-range algorithm

import { useMemo } from "react";

// Returns e.g. [1, "…", 4, 5, 6, "…", 20]. siblingCount controls neighbors.
function getPageRange({ current, total, siblingCount = 1 }) {
  const totalNumbers = siblingCount * 2 + 5; // first, last, current, 2 dots
  if (total <= totalNumbers) return Array.from({ length: total }, (_, i) => i + 1);

  const left = Math.max(current - siblingCount, 1);
  const right = Math.min(current + siblingCount, total);
  const showLeftDots = left > 2;
  const showRightDots = right < total - 1;

  const range = (s, e) => Array.from({ length: e - s + 1 }, (_, i) => s + i);

  if (!showLeftDots && showRightDots) return [...range(1, 3 + 2 * siblingCount), "…", total];
  if (showLeftDots && !showRightDots) return [1, "…", ...range(total - (2 + 2 * siblingCount), total)];
  return [1, "…", ...range(left, right), "…", total];
}

export function Pagination({ current, total, onChange, siblingCount = 1 }) {
  const pages = useMemo(
    () => getPageRange({ current, total, siblingCount }),
    [current, total, siblingCount]
  );
  if (total <= 1) return null;

  return (
    <nav role="navigation" aria-label="Pagination">
      <ul style={{ display: "flex", listStyle: "none", gap: 4 }}>
        <li>
          <button onClick={() => onChange(current - 1)} disabled={current === 1} aria-label="Previous page">‹</button>
        </li>
        {pages.map((p, i) =>
          p === "…" ? (
            <li key={`dots-${i}`} aria-hidden="true">…</li>
          ) : (
            <li key={p}>
              <button
                onClick={() => onChange(p)}
                aria-current={p === current ? "page" : undefined}
                aria-label={`${p === current ? "Current page, " : "Go to "}page ${p}`}
              >
                {p}
              </button>
            </li>
          )
        )}
        <li>
          <button onClick={() => onChange(current + 1)} disabled={current === total} aria-label="Next page">›</button>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • The range algorithm is the whole test: handle "too few pages to truncate", left-only dots, right-only dots, both-sides dots. Stable count prevents the control from jumping width as you page.
  • a11y: <nav aria-label="Pagination">, aria-current="page" (not just a class) on the active page, labeled prev/next, ellipses aria-hidden (they convey nothing).
  • Controlled component: current/onChange — parent owns state and syncs to URL query (?page=4) for shareable/back-button-able pagination.
  • Edge cases: single page (render nothing), disable prev on page 1 / next on last, large total (50k pages) still renders ≤ ~9 buttons.
  • "30 more minutes": keyboard arrow nav, jump-to-page input, page-size selector, prefetch next page on hover, cursor pagination for infinite datasets.

2.9 Drag-and-drop list

  • HTML5 drag events OR Pointer events for full control.
  • Drag preview; calculate insertion index by measuring rects.
  • A11y: Space lift, Arrow move, Space drop, Esc cancel.

Complete implementation (HTML5 DnD + keyboard alternative)

import { useState, useRef, useCallback } from "react";

export function SortableList({ items: initial, onReorder }) {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(initial);
  const [dragIndex, setDragIndex] = useState(null);
  const [overIndex, setOverIndex] = useState(null);
  const [lifted, setLifted] = useState(null); // index being moved via keyboard
  const listRef = useRef(null);

  const announce = msg => {
    const region = document.getElementById("dnd-live");
    if (region) region.textContent = msg;
  };

  const move = useCallback((from, to) => {
    if (from == null || from === to || to < 0 || to >= items.length) return;
    setItems(prev => {
      const next = prev.slice();
      const [moved] = next.splice(from, 1);
      next.splice(to, 0, moved);
      onReorder?.(next);
      return next;
    });
  }, [items.length, onReorder]);

  // --- Pointer DnD ---
  const onDragStart = (e, i) => { setDragIndex(i); e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = "move"; };
  const onDragOver = (e, i) => { e.preventDefault(); setOverIndex(i); }; // preventDefault enables drop
  const onDrop = (e, i) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    move(dragIndex, i);
    setDragIndex(null); setOverIndex(null);
  };
  const onDragEnd = () => { setDragIndex(null); setOverIndex(null); };

  // --- Keyboard DnD ---
  const onKeyDown = (e, i) => {
    if (e.key === " " || e.key === "Enter") {
      e.preventDefault();
      if (lifted === null) {
        setLifted(i);
        announce(`Lifted item ${i + 1}. Use arrow keys to move, space to drop.`);
      } else {
        announce(`Dropped at position ${i + 1}.`);
        setLifted(null);
      }
    } else if (lifted !== null && (e.key === "ArrowUp" || e.key === "ArrowDown")) {
      e.preventDefault();
      const to = lifted + (e.key === "ArrowDown" ? 1 : -1);
      if (to < 0 || to >= items.length) return;
      move(lifted, to);
      setLifted(to);
      announce(`Moved to position ${to + 1} of ${items.length}.`);
      requestAnimationFrame(() => listRef.current?.querySelectorAll("li")[to]?.focus());
    } else if (e.key === "Escape" && lifted !== null) {
      setLifted(null);
      announce("Cancelled.");
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
      <ul ref={listRef} role="list" aria-label="Sortable list">
        {items.map((item, i) => (
          <li
            key={item.id}
            tabIndex={0}
            draggable
            aria-grabbed={dragIndex === i || lifted === i}
            onDragStart={e => onDragStart(e, i)}
            onDragOver={e => onDragOver(e, i)}
            onDrop={e => onDrop(e, i)}
            onDragEnd={onDragEnd}
            onKeyDown={e => onKeyDown(e, i)}
            style={{
              opacity: dragIndex === i ? 0.4 : 1,
              outline: overIndex === i ? "2px dashed #888" : lifted === i ? "2px solid #06f" : "none",
            }}
          >
            {item.label}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <div id="dnd-live" role="status" aria-live="assertive" className="sr-only" />
    </>
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • HTML5 DnD gotchas: must e.preventDefault() in onDragOver or onDrop never fires; dataTransfer.effectAllowed; the native drag image is the row by default. Pointer Events give pixel-perfect control + touch but you reimplement everything.
  • Insertion index: for finer drops, measure getBoundingClientRect() of each row and compare pointer Y to each midpoint to decide before/after — shown here simplified to drop-on-target.
  • Accessibility is the senior differentiator: native HTML5 DnD is *not* keyboard accessible at all. Provide the full keyboard protocol — Space to lift, arrows to move, Space to drop, Esc to cancel — with an aria-live="assertive" region announcing every move. aria-grabbed for the lifted item.
  • Immutability: reorder via splice on a copy; controlled-ish with onReorder callback.
  • Edge cases: drop on self (no-op), boundary moves, dragging the last item, dropping outside the list.
  • "30 more minutes": auto-scroll when dragging near edges, drag handle vs whole-row, multi-list (kanban) transfer, FLIP animations, @dnd-kit in production (accessible + performant) instead of hand-rolling.

2.10 Form wizard with validation

  • Steps stored in URL search params (back/forward works).
  • Schema-first with Zod; mirror to UI.
  • Save progress to localStorage; "Resume?" on revisit.

Complete implementation (multi-step, per-step validation, persistence)

import { useState, useCallback, useEffect, useMemo } from "react";
import { z } from "zod";

const stepSchemas = [
  z.object({ name: z.string().min(1, "Name is required"), email: z.string().email("Invalid email") }),
  z.object({ street: z.string().min(1, "Street required"), city: z.string().min(1, "City required") }),
  z.object({ plan: z.enum(["basic", "pro"], { message: "Pick a plan" }) }),
];
const STORAGE_KEY = "wizard:draft";

function useStepParam(maxStep) {
  const read = () => {
    const n = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("step") ?? 0);
    return Number.isInteger(n) ? Math.min(Math.max(n, 0), maxStep) : 0;
  };
  const [step, setStepState] = useState(read);
  const setStep = useCallback(next => {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
    params.set("step", String(next));
    history.pushState({}, "", `?${params}`); // back/forward navigates steps
    setStepState(next);
  }, []);
  useEffect(() => {
    const onPop = () => setStepState(read());
    addEventListener("popstate", onPop);
    return () => removeEventListener("popstate", onPop);
  }, []); // eslint-disable-line
  return [step, setStep];
}

export function FormWizard({ onComplete }) {
  const [step, setStep] = useStepParam(stepSchemas.length - 1);
  const [data, setData] = useState(() => {
    try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) ?? "{}"); }
    catch { return {}; }
  });
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState({});
  const [resumePrompt, setResumePrompt] = useState(
    () => Object.keys(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) ?? "{}")).length > 0
  );

  // Persist on every change (debounce in prod).
  useEffect(() => { localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(data)); }, [data]);

  const update = (field, value) => setData(d => ({ ...d, [field]: value }));

  const validateStep = useCallback(() => {
    const result = stepSchemas[step].safeParse(data);
    if (result.success) { setErrors({}); return true; }
    const fieldErrors = {};
    for (const issue of result.error.issues) fieldErrors[issue.path[0]] = issue.message;
    setErrors(fieldErrors);
    return false;
  }, [step, data]);

  const next = () => {
    if (!validateStep()) return;
    if (step === stepSchemas.length - 1) {
      localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
      onComplete?.(data);
    } else setStep(step + 1);
  };
  const back = () => setStep(Math.max(0, step - 1));

  const fields = useMemo(() => Object.keys(stepSchemas[step].shape), [step]);

  if (resumePrompt) {
    return (
      <div role="dialog" aria-label="Resume draft">
        <p>You have a saved draft. Resume?</p>
        <button onClick={() => setResumePrompt(false)}>Resume</button>
        <button onClick={() => { setData({}); localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY); setResumePrompt(false); }}>
          Start over
        </button>
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={e => { e.preventDefault(); next(); }} noValidate>
      <ol aria-label="Progress" style={{ display: "flex", gap: 8 }}>
        {stepSchemas.map((_, i) => (
          <li key={i} aria-current={i === step ? "step" : undefined}>
            Step {i + 1}{i === step ? " (current)" : ""}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ol>

      {fields.map(field => (
        <div key={field}>
          <label htmlFor={field}>{field}</label>
          <input
            id={field}
            value={data[field] ?? ""}
            onChange={e => update(field, e.target.value)}
            aria-invalid={!!errors[field]}
            aria-describedby={errors[field] ? `${field}-err` : undefined}
          />
          {errors[field] && <p id={`${field}-err`} role="alert">{errors[field]}</p>}
        </div>
      ))}

      <div>
        <button type="button" onClick={back} disabled={step === 0}>Back</button>
        <button type="submit">{step === stepSchemas.length - 1 ? "Submit" : "Next"}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  );
}

Senior talking points:

  • Schema-first: Zod is the single source of truth — validation messages, types (z.infer), and which fields render all derive from the schema. Per-step safeParse so you only validate the current step's slice.
  • URL as state: ?step=2 makes browser back/forward move between steps and the link shareable; popstate listener keeps React in sync. This is the detail that impresses.
  • Persistence + resume: autosave to localStorage (debounced in prod), clear on submit, "Resume draft?" gate on remount. Mention privacy — don't persist sensitive fields (passwords, PII) to localStorage.
  • a11y: labeled inputs, aria-invalid + aria-describedby linking the error, role="alert" for live error announcement, aria-current="step", noValidate to use custom messages.
  • Edge cases: deep-linking to an invalid step (clamp), back from step 0, refreshing mid-wizard, validation on blur vs on submit.
  • "30 more minutes": conditional/branching steps, async validation (email uniqueness) with debounce, focus-first-error on failed submit, optimistic submit + rollback, react-hook-form + zodResolver in production.

Part 3 — 50 daily drills

How to use: time-box each to 20–30 min. Day 1 write it, Day 2 add edge cases + tests, periodically redo from scratch. Group by week: Promises/async, functional utils, data structures, components, TypeScript types. Track which you can do cold in <20 min — those are interview-ready.

  • Promise.all without library; handle empty input.
  • Promise.race; explain why empty input hangs.
  • debounce with cancel + flush.
  • throttle (trailing edge).
  • curry that supports both forms.
  • Function.prototype.bind with new semantics.
  • deepClone with cycle support.
  • deepEqual; handle Map and Set.
  • memoize with custom key + LRU.
  • EventEmitter with once + off + return-unsubscribe.
  • retry-with-exponential-backoff utility.
  • LRU cache (Map iteration order trick).
  • pub/sub with namespaces.
  • Typeahead with cancel + race-guard.
  • Infinite-scroll list with IntersectionObserver.
  • Modal with focus trap.
  • Toast provider.
  • Star rating component.
  • Multi-select autocomplete with chips.
  • Kanban board with DnD + keyboard alt.
  • Accordion with proper ARIA.
  • Pagination with ellipses.
  • Multi-step form wizard with URL state.
  • Date picker (no library) with a11y.
  • Virtual list for 100K items.
  • Tic-tac-toe with bot.
  • Snake on canvas.
  • Sudoku solver UI.
  • Stopwatch with lap times.
  • Polling with backoff + pause-on-hidden.
  • State machine as discriminated union.
  • Author DeepReadonly<T>.
  • Author DeepPartial<T>.
  • Author UnionToTuple<U>.
  • Author RouteParams<"/users/:id/posts/:pid">.
  • Author Brand<T, "Email"> + validator.
  • Author Equals<X, Y> + static assertion.
  • Typed fetch wrapper inferring response from URL.
  • Typed event bus inferring payload type from map.
  • Zod-like schema as a TS generic.
  • useFetch with abort + retry + cache.
  • Offline queue that retries on online.
  • Trie for autocomplete.
  • Calculator with operator precedence.
  • Promise pool (concurrency cap).
  • timeout(promise, ms).
  • once(fn) — runs once, caches result.
  • diff(a, b) returning JSON-Patch-style ops.
  • structured-clone-ish for serialization.
  • Tiny middleware pipeline.

Three reference solutions for the trickiest drills

// Promise.all from scratch — order-preserving, empty-safe, fail-fast.
function promiseAll(promises) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const list = [...promises];
    if (list.length === 0) return resolve([]); // empty must resolve, not hang
    const results = new Array(list.length);
    let remaining = list.length;
    list.forEach((p, i) => {
      Promise.resolve(p).then(
        value => { results[i] = value; if (--remaining === 0) resolve(results); },
        reject // first rejection wins
      );
    });
  });
}

// debounce with cancel + flush.
function debounce(fn, wait) {
  let timer = null, lastArgs = null, lastThis = null;
  function debounced(...args) {
    lastArgs = args; lastThis = this;
    clearTimeout(timer);
    timer = setTimeout(() => { fn.apply(lastThis, lastArgs); timer = null; }, wait);
  }
  debounced.cancel = () => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = null; };
  debounced.flush = () => {
    if (timer) { clearTimeout(timer); fn.apply(lastThis, lastArgs); timer = null; }
  };
  return debounced;
}

// Tiny middleware pipeline (Express/Koa/Redux style) — onion model with next().
function createPipeline() {
  const middleware = [];
  return {
    use(fn) { middleware.push(fn); return this; },
    run(ctx) {
      let index = -1;
      function dispatch(i) {
        if (i <= index) return Promise.reject(new Error("next() called multiple times"));
        index = i;
        const fn = middleware[i];
        if (!fn) return Promise.resolve();
        return Promise.resolve(fn(ctx, () => dispatch(i + 1)));
      }
      return dispatch(0);
    },
  };
}
