12 — FE Tools Catalog Volume II (UI libs · Design · AI · Mobile · Automation)

Volume II — 30 more categories · 250+ libraries and services · with OSS alternatives

Continuation of Doc 11. Where Doc 11 catalogs services (auth, payments, observability, CMS), this one covers what you actually wire into your code (UI libraries, charts, editors), plus the creative + AI + mobile tooling teams use day-to-day.

> How to read this volume: every category keeps its original quick-reference list, then adds a decision matrix (tool → strengths → when to pick), one real, buildable snippet for the leading pick, and the senior gotcha that bites in code review (bundle size, RSC compatibility, a11y, SSR/hydration). Code is 2026-accurate: React 19, Next.js 15 App Router, Tailwind v4, RSC by default.

Part 1 — UI Component Libraries

1.1 Headless (you bring the styles)

LibraryStrengthNote
Radix PrimitivesBest a11y, unstyled, composableFoundation under shadcn/ui
React Aria (Adobe)Industry-best a11y, hooks-basedHeavier API; use react-aria-components
Headless UI (Tailwind Labs)Tight Tailwind integrationSmaller surface than Radix
AriakitComposable primitives + stateOSS, accessible, flexible
Base UI (MUI)Headless side of MUIGood if migrating from MUI
TanStack componentsTanStack Table, Virtual, FormHeadless data layer

Decision matrix

PickStrengthsWhen to pick
Radix PrimitivesSmallest correct a11y surface, controlled/uncontrolled, asChild slot compositionDefault headless base; you (or shadcn) own all styling
React Aria ComponentsMost rigorous a11y (Adobe spends real money on it), i18n-aware, mobile/touch correctDate pickers, comboboxes, complex grids, regulated/enterprise a11y bars
Base UISame team as Radix maintainers now; modern API, MUI lineageGreenfield where you want Radix ergonomics with a single vendor roadmap
Headless UIZero-config Tailwind transitions, tiny surfaceTailwind-only app needing just Menu/Dialog/Combobox
AriakitMost flexible state model, huge component countYou need primitives Radix lacks (e.g. complex composite widgets)

Real usage — Radix Dialog, fully unstyled + accessible

"use client";
import * as Dialog from "@radix-ui/react-dialog";

export function ConfirmDialog({ onConfirm }: { onConfirm: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Dialog.Root>
      <Dialog.Trigger className="rounded bg-red-600 px-3 py-1.5 text-white">
        Delete
      </Dialog.Trigger>
      <Dialog.Portal>
        <Dialog.Overlay className="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50 data-[state=open]:animate-in" />
        <Dialog.Content
          className="fixed left-1/2 top-1/2 w-80 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2
                     rounded-lg bg-white p-6 shadow-xl focus:outline-none"
          // Radix wires aria-labelledby/aria-describedby from Title/Description automatically
        >
          <Dialog.Title className="text-lg font-semibold">Delete item?</Dialog.Title>
          <Dialog.Description className="mt-1 text-sm text-gray-500">
            This action cannot be undone.
          </Dialog.Description>
          <div className="mt-4 flex justify-end gap-2">
            <Dialog.Close className="px-3 py-1.5">Cancel</Dialog.Close>
            <Dialog.Close
              onClick={onConfirm}
              className="rounded bg-red-600 px-3 py-1.5 text-white"
            >
              Delete
            </Dialog.Close>
          </div>
        </Dialog.Content>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </Dialog.Root>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: Every Radix/React-Aria primitive ships hooks and portals, so it is a Client Component — the "use client" boundary cascades to everything you nest inside Dialog.Content. Keep the interactive shell in a leaf client component and pass server-rendered content in as children/props so you don't accidentally pull your whole tree out of RSC. Also: a Dialog.Title is required for screen-reader labeling — omitting it throws a dev warning and ships a broken a11y tree. Radix portals render at document.body, which breaks overflow-hidden clipping and any CSS-variable theme scoped to a subtree; re-declare theme vars on the portal or use Radix's container prop.

1.2 Styled component kits

KitApproachSweet spot
shadcn/uiCopy-paste Radix + Tailwind code into your repoDefault in 2026; full control + speed
NextUIReact + Tailwind, themeableBeautiful defaults; opinionated
MantineFull React UI kit, includes hooksMid-market SaaS dashboards
Chakra UIStyle props + simple APIQuick prototypes, internal tools
Material UI (MUI)Google Material specEnterprise + Material-language apps
Ant DesignEnterprise-grade, opinionatedAdmin dashboards, China-friendly
TremorCharts + dashboardsInternal analytics dashboards
Park UIArk UI + Panda CSSDevs who want shadcn-style for Vue/Svelte too
daisyUITailwind component classesQuick projects; small bundle
FlowbiteTailwind + Alpine + React + VueMarketing + dashboards
Preline UITailwind componentsFree + premium variants

Decision matrix

PickStrengthsWhen to pick
shadcn/uiYou own the source; no version-lock; Tailwind v4 + Radix; CLI scaffolds into your repoDefault 2026 for product UIs that will be customized heavily
Mantine v7+Batteries-included (100+ components, 50+ hooks), CSS-modules (RSC-safe), forms, dates, chartsDashboards where velocity beats pixel-perfect bespoke design
MUI v6Material spec, enterprise component depth (DataGrid, X-charts), strong a11yEnterprise/Material-language apps, internal tools with budget
Ant Design v5Densest enterprise component set, design tokens, formsAdmin consoles, data-heavy back office
Chakra UI v3Ergonomic style props, themingPrototypes/internal tools (note v3 moved to Ark UI + Panda underneath)
NextUI / HeroUIGorgeous defaults, Tailwind-native, motion built inMarketing-grade product UIs wanting opinionated polish

Real usage — shadcn/ui button with cva variants (the canonical pattern)

import { cva, type VariantProps } from "class-variance-authority";
import { Slot } from "@radix-ui/react-slot";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"; // cn = twMerge(clsx(...))

const buttonVariants = cva(
  "inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md text-sm font-medium " +
    "transition-colors focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 disabled:opacity-50",
  {
    variants: {
      variant: {
        default: "bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90",
        outline: "border border-input bg-background hover:bg-accent",
        ghost: "hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground",
      },
      size: { sm: "h-8 px-3", md: "h-9 px-4", lg: "h-10 px-6" },
    },
    defaultVariants: { variant: "default", size: "md" },
  },
);

type Props = React.ComponentProps<"button"> &
  VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> & { asChild?: boolean };

export function Button({ className, variant, size, asChild, ...props }: Props) {
  const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button";
  return <Comp className={cn(buttonVariants({ variant, size, className }))} {...props} />;
}

Senior gotcha: Runtime CSS-in-JS kits (MUI v5 Emotion, older Chakra) inject styles at render and are not RSC-compatible without an SSR style-registry shim — you get FOUC or a hydration mismatch in App Router. Prefer kits already on zero-runtime/CSS-modules (Mantine v7, Chakra v3/Panda, shadcn/Tailwind). With shadcn, the cn() helper must be twMerge(clsx(...)) or conflicting utilities (px-3 + px-4) won't dedupe and last-write-wins breaks variants. Don't npm i a kit "just for one Button" — a full kit (Ant, MUI) can add 100–300 KB gzip; reach for shadcn copy-paste or a headless primitive instead.

1.3 Premium / commercial component kits

  • Tailwind UI / Catalyst — official Tailwind components (subscription).
  • Magic UI — animated marketing components (free + pro).
  • Aceternity UI — heavy animation + AI-style components.
  • Cult UI — copy-paste advanced React components.
  • Untitled UI — Figma-based design system; React port.
  • Material Tailwind Pro — Material + Tailwind premium.
  • Tailgrids — broad marketing UI.
  • Konsta UI — iOS / Material mobile-feel components.

Decision matrix

PickStrengthsWhen to pick
Tailwind UI / CatalystFirst-party, accessible, maintained by Tailwind Labs; React + HTMLMarketing pages + app shells where you want vetted markup fast
Aceternity / Magic UIHeavy Framer Motion eye-candy, copy-pasteLanding pages, AI-product hero sections that need "wow"
Untitled UIMassive Figma kit with React parityDesign-led teams syncing Figma → code
Konsta UIiOS/Material native feel on webCapacitor/PWA apps that must feel native

Senior gotcha: Animation-heavy premium kits (Aceternity, Magic UI) pull in Framer Motion + often a 3D dep per component; a single hero can add 80–150 KB and tank LCP/INP on mobile. Treat them as marketing-page-only — lazy-load with next/dynamic({ ssr: false }), and never ship them in the authenticated app bundle. Also audit licenses: "copy-paste" kits often relicense MIT components you could get free; pay for the design, not the code.

1.4 Senior gotchas

  • Component libs bloat fast — measure the bundle impact of every import.
  • shadcn (copy-paste) > npm component lib if you need to customize heavily.
  • Lock dark mode + theming early; refactor later is painful.
  • Accessibility regressions are easy when restyling; test with axe before shipping.

Expanded checklist

  • Measure, don't guess. Wire @next/bundle-analyzer or vite-bundle-visualizer into CI and fail PRs that grow the entry chunk past a budget. Barrel imports (import { X } from "lib") often defeat tree-shaking — import from the deep path.
  • RSC boundary discipline. Any interactive primitive is a client component; keep them as leaves and pass server data as props. A stray "use client" at the top of a layout poisons the whole subtree.
  • Theme tokens once. Define color/spacing/radius as CSS variables (Tailwind v4 @theme) so dark mode is a .dark class flip, not a per-component rewrite. shadcn's tweakcn generates these.
  • a11y in CI, not vibes. Run axe-core via Playwright on key flows; restyling a focus ring or removing an outline silently regresses keyboard users.
  • Hydration safety. Anything reading window, localStorage, or Date.now() at render must be gated to useEffect or ssr: false, or you get the dreaded text-content-mismatch.

  • Tailwind CSS — dominant 2026; v4 is significantly faster.
  • UnoCSS — Tailwind-compatible, infinite extensibility, faster.

  • Tachyons — minimal utility framework (legacy).

Real usage — Tailwind v4 CSS-first config (no tailwind.config.js)

/* app/globals.css */
@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  --color-brand-500: oklch(0.62 0.19 255);
  --color-brand-600: oklch(0.55 0.20 255);

Senior gotcha: Tailwind v4 dropped the JS config and PostCSS content globbing for a Rust scanner — but it still only sees classes that appear as complete static strings in your source. Dynamically built classes (` bg-${color}-500 ) get purged out of the production CSS and silently vanish. Use a cva/tailwind-variants` map or safelist them. The v3→v4 migration also renames the config surface and changes default color space to OKLCH, so a blind upgrade shifts every color slightly.

// panda recipe → compiles to atomic CSS at build time
import { cva } from "../styled-system/css";

export const badge = cva({
  base: { display: "inline-flex", borderRadius: "md", px: "2", fontSize: "sm" },

Senior gotcha: styled-components and Emotion's css prop execute at render time on the client, so in Next.js App Router they require a Client Component boundary plus an SSR style registry, and they still cause a flash or hydration mismatch under streaming/PPR. They are effectively deprecated for new code. Migrate to a zero-runtime extractor (Panda, Vanilla Extract, Linaria, StyleX) or Tailwind. "use client";
import {
  LineChart, Line, XAxis, YAxis, Tooltip, ResponsiveContainer, CartesianGrid,
} from "recharts";

type Point = { date: string; mrr: number };

export function MrrChart({ data }: { data: Point[] }) {
  return (
    <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height={280}>
      <LineChart data={data} margin={{ top: 8, right: 16, bottom: 0, left: 0 }}>

Senior gotcha: Recharts is SVG — every datapoint is a DOM node, so it grinds past a few thousand points; switch to canvas (ECharts) or uPlot for large/live series. It also can't measure container size on the server, so ResponsiveContainer renders 0×0 during SSR and pops in on hydration (CLS) — give it a fixed height and an explicit min-width, or gate with ssr: false. Disable isAnimationActive for dashboards that re-render on data updates, or you'll re-trigger a 1s animation on every poll.

Real usage — TanStack Table column defs + render

"use client";
import {
  useReactTable, getCoreRowModel, getSortedRowModel,
  flexRender, type ColumnDef, type SortingState,
} from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { useState } from "react";

type User = { id: string; name: string; email: string; mrr: number };

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
  { accessorKey: "email", header: "Email" },
  {
    accessorKey: "mrr",
    header: "MRR",
    cell: (info) => `$${info.getValue<number>().toLocaleString()}`,
  },
];

export function UsersTable({ data }: { data: User[] }) {
  const [sorting, setSorting] = useState<SortingState>([]);
  const table = useReactTable({
    data, columns, state: { sorting }, onSortingChange: setSorting,
    getCoreRowModel: getCoreRowModel(), getSortedRowModel: getSortedRowModel(),
  });

  return (
    <table className="w-full text-sm">
      <thead>
        {table.getHeaderGroups().map((hg) => (
          <tr key={hg.id}>
            {hg.headers.map((h) => (
              <th key={h.id} onClick={h.column.getToggleSortingHandler()}
                  className="cursor-pointer px-3 py-2 text-left">
                {flexRender(h.column.columnDef.header, h.getContext())}
                {{ asc: " ↑", desc: " ↓" }[h.column.getIsSorted() as string] ?? ""}
              </th>
            ))}
          </tr>
        ))}
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {table.getRowModel().rows.map((row) => (
          <tr key={row.id} className="border-t">
            {row.getVisibleCells().map((cell) => (
              <td key={cell.id} className="px-3 py-2">
                {flexRender(cell.column.columnDef.cell ?? cell.column.columnDef.header, cell.getContext())}
              </td>
            ))}
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: TanStack Table renders every row to the DOM by default — it does not virtualize. For 1K+ rows pair it with @tanstack/react-virtual or you'll freeze the main thread. Also: define columns outside the component or in useMemo with a stable reference; recreating the array each render thrashes the table's internal memoization and re-runs sorting/filtering on every keystroke. AG Grid's advanced features (pivot, server-side row model) are behind the Enterprise license — using them without a key shows a watermark and is a compliance risk.

Real usage — Tiptap minimal editor

"use client";
import { useEditor, EditorContent } from "@tiptap/react";
import StarterKit from "@tiptap/starter-kit";

export function Editor({ onChange }: { onChange?: (html: string) => void }) {
  const editor = useEditor({
    extensions: [StarterKit],
    content: "<p>Write something…</p>",
    immediatelyRender: false, // REQUIRED in Next.js App Router to avoid SSR hydration mismatch
    onUpdate: ({ editor }) => onChange?.(editor.getHTML()),
    editorProps: { attributes: { class: "prose max-w-none focus:outline-none" } },
  });

  if (!editor) return null;
  return (
    <div className="rounded border p-3">
      <div className="mb-2 flex gap-1">
        <button
          onClick={() => editor.chain().focus().toggleBold().run()}
          className={editor.isActive("bold") ? "font-bold underline" : ""}
        >
          B
        </button>
        <button
          onClick={() => editor.chain().focus().toggleBulletList().run()}
          className={editor.isActive("bulletList") ? "underline" : ""}
        >
          • List
        </button>
      </div>
      <EditorContent editor={editor} />
    </div>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: Tiptap (and all ProseMirror/Lexical editors) touch the DOM on init, so in App Router you must set immediatelyRender: false or you get a hydration mismatch crash. The editor is inherently a Client Component — keep it a leaf and render server content into it. For persistence, store ProseMirror JSON, not HTML: HTML round-trips lossily and is harder to migrate/sanitize. If you accept HTML from users, sanitize on the server (DOMPurify) before render to avoid stored XSS. Collab via Yjs adds a CRDT doc + websocket provider — meaningful bundle and infra; don't add it speculatively.

import { ReactFlow, Background, Controls, type Node, type Edge } from "@xyflow/react";
import "@xyflow/react/dist/style.css";

const nodes: Node[] = [
  { id: "1", position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, data: { label: "Trigger" } },

  { id: "3", position: { x: 400, y: 0 }, data: { label: "Output" } },

Senior gotcha: React Flow requires its parent to have an explicit width/height (it measures via ResizeObserver); drop it in an auto-height flex child and you get a 0px canvas that renders nothing — a classic "it works in the demo but not my app" bug. Real usage — react-pdf page render

"use client";
import { Document, Page, pdfjs } from "react-pdf";
import "react-pdf/dist/Page/TextLayer.css";
import { useState } from "react";

// Pin the worker to a matching version (CDN or self-hosted)
pdfjs.GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc = `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pdfjs-dist@${pdfjs.version}/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs`;

export function PdfViewer({ url }: { url: string }) {
  const [pages, setPages] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Document file={url} onLoadSuccess={({ numPages }) => setPages(numPages)}>
      {Array.from({ length: pages }, (_, i) => (
        <Page key={i} pageNumber={i + 1} width={640} />
      ))}
    </Document>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: PDF.js runs in a web worker and the worker version must exactly match the main-thread pdfjs-dist version, or you get cryptic "API/Worker version mismatch" failures — pin both. The worker also needs correct bundler config (new URL(..., import.meta.url) or a copied asset); CDN-loading the worker is the reliable cross-bundler escape hatch. PDF.js is heavy (~1 MB+) — lazy-load and never SSR it (ssr: false).

Real usage — Motion enter/exit + layout animation

"use client";
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";

export function Toast({ open, msg }: { open: boolean; msg: string }) {
  return (
    <AnimatePresence>
      {open && (
        <motion.div
          layout
          initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 12, scale: 0.98 }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, scale: 1 }}
          exit={{ opacity: 0, y: 12, scale: 0.98 }}
          transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 30 }}
          className="rounded-lg bg-gray-900 px-4 py-2 text-white shadow-lg"
        >
          {msg}
        </motion.div>
      )}
    </AnimatePresence>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: motion is a Client Component library and a full import is ~30–40 KB; use LazyMotion + m components to defer the feature bundle, and never animate width/height/top (layout-thrashing) — animate transform/opacity so the work stays on the compositor and INP stays low. AnimatePresence only animates exit if the element is its direct child with a stable key; conditionally rendered grandchildren won't exit-animate. Always respect prefers-reduced-motion (Motion exposes useReducedMotion()), or you fail WCAG 2.3.3.

"use client";
import { DndContext, closestCenter, type DragEndEvent } from "@dnd-kit/core";
import {
  SortableContext, useSortable, verticalListSortingStrategy, arrayMove,
} from "@dnd-kit/sortable";
import { CSS } from "@dnd-kit/utilities";
import { useState } from "react";

function Item({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const { attributes, listeners, setNodeRef, transform, transition } = useSortable({ id });
  return (
    <li ref={setNodeRef} {...attributes} {...listeners}
        style={{ transform: CSS.Transform.toString(transform), transition }}
        className="cursor-grab rounded border bg-white px-3 py-2">
      {id}
    </li>
  );
}

export function SortableList() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(["a", "b", "c", "d"]);
  function onDragEnd({ active, over }: DragEndEvent) {
    if (over && active.id !== over.id) {
      setItems((it) => arrayMove(it, it.indexOf(active.id as string), it.indexOf(over.id as string)));
    }
  }
  return (
    <DndContext collisionDetection={closestCenter} onDragEnd={onDragEnd}>
      <SortableContext items={items} strategy={verticalListSortingStrategy}>
        <ul className="space-y-1">{items.map((id) => <Item key={id} id={id} />)}</ul>
      </SortableContext>
    </DndContext>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: react-beautiful-dnd is archived — do not start new work on it; use @hello-pangea/dnd (its maintained fork) or dnd-kit. dnd-kit needs stable, unique item IDs (array index as id breaks reordering). For accessibility, dnd-kit ships keyboard sensors but you must provide screen-reader announcements; don't ship pointer-only DnD. SSR: drag state is client-only — render the static list on the server and hydrate the DnD context as a leaf client component.

"use client";
import { Canvas, useFrame } from "@react-three/fiber";
import { OrbitControls, Environment } from "@react-three/drei";
import { useRef } from "react";
import type { Mesh } from "three";

function SpinningBox() {
  const ref = useRef<Mesh>(null!);
  useFrame((_, dt) => { ref.current.rotation.y += dt * 0.6; });
  return (
    <mesh ref={ref}>
      <boxGeometry args={[1, 1, 1]} />
      <meshStandardMaterial color="#6366f1" />

export function Scene() {
  return (
    <Canvas camera={{ position: [3, 2, 4] }} style={{ height: 400 }}>
      <ambientLight intensity={0.6} />

      <Environment preset="city" />

}

Senior gotcha: <Canvas> and everything under it is client-only — it cannot SSR (no WebGL on the server), so wrap with next/dynamic({ ssr: false }) and a loading fallback. Three.js + drei is large (~150 KB+ and model assets dwarf it); lazy-load per route and compress models to .glb/Draco/KTX2. Manage WebGL context loss and dispose geometries/materials on unmount or you leak GPU memory across route changes. useFrame runs every frame — keep it allocation-free (no new Vector3() per frame).

Real usage — WebGPU capability gate

export async function getGpu(): Promise<GPUDevice | null> {
  if (!("gpu" in navigator)) return null; // older browsers: fall back to WebGL
  const adapter = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();
  if (!adapter) return null;             // low-power GPUs can return null
  return adapter.requestDevice();
}

Senior gotcha: WebGPU is stable in Chromium and Safari but still gated/flagged in some browsers and most older devices in 2026 — always feature-detect navigator.gpu and keep a WebGL/WASM fallback path. It also requires a secure context (HTTPS) and can be disabled by enterprise policy. Don't assume requestAdapter() succeeds; on low-power GPUs it returns null.

Real usage — React Hook Form + Zod resolver

"use client";
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
import { z } from "zod";

const schema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email("Enter a valid email"),
  password: z.string().min(8, "Min 8 characters"),
});
type FormData = z.infer<typeof schema>;

export function SignupForm() {
  const { register, handleSubmit, formState: { errors, isSubmitting } } =
    useForm<FormData>({ resolver: zodResolver(schema) });

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(async (data) => { await api.signup(data); })}
          className="space-y-3">
      <div>
        <input {...register("email")} placeholder="Email" className="w-full rounded border px-3 py-2" />
        {errors.email && <p className="text-sm text-red-600">{errors.email.message}</p>}
      </div>
      <div>
        <input type="password" {...register("password")} placeholder="Password"
               className="w-full rounded border px-3 py-2" />
        {errors.password && <p className="text-sm text-red-600">{errors.password.message}</p>}
      </div>
      <button disabled={isSubmitting} className="rounded bg-black px-4 py-2 text-white">
        {isSubmitting ? "Creating…" : "Create account"}
      </button>
    </form>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: RHF's register relies on uncontrolled inputs; wrapping a third-party controlled component (MUI Select, Radix) requires the <Controller> adapter, and forgetting it gives you a field that "doesn't submit." Client-side validation is UX, not security — always re-validate the same Zod schema on the server (Server Action or API) because anyone can bypass the client. In App Router, prefer Conform when the form must submit without JS (progressive enhancement); RHF requires hydration to work.

import { z } from "zod";

export const CreatePost = z.object({
  title: z.string().min(1).max(120),
  body: z.string().min(1),
  tags: z.array(z.string()).max(5).default([]),
});
export type CreatePost = z.infer<typeof CreatePost>;

// server action:
export async function createPost(raw: unknown) {
  "use server";
  const data = CreatePost.parse(raw); // throws on bad input — never trust the client
  return db.post.create({ data });
}

Senior gotcha: Zod's bundle is dominated by the fact it's not fully tree-shakeable (much of the library comes along), so on bundle-critical client paths Valibot/ArkType win — but keep one source of truth and validate the same shape on the server regardless. Avoid recreating schemas inside render/handlers (allocates on every call); define them at module scope. JSON-Schema validators (Ajv) need a compile step and can leak if you compile() per request — compile once and cache.

Real usage — react-dropzone + presigned S3 upload

"use client";
import { useDropzone } from "react-dropzone";

export function Uploader() {
  const { getRootProps, getInputProps, isDragActive } = useDropzone({
    accept: { "image/*": [] },
    maxSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
    onDrop: async (files) => {
      for (const file of files) {
        const { url } = await fetch("/api/presign", {
          method: "POST",
          body: JSON.stringify({ name: file.name, type: file.type }),
        }).then((r) => r.json());
        await fetch(url, { method: "PUT", body: file }); // direct-to-S3, bypasses your server
      }
    },
  });
  return (
    <div {...getRootProps()} className="cursor-pointer rounded border-2 border-dashed p-8 text-center">
      <input {...getInputProps()} />
      {isDragActive ? "Drop files…" : "Drag files or click to browse"}
    </div>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: Never proxy large files through your Next.js/serverless function — App Router bodies and serverless platforms cap request size (often 4–6 MB) and you'll OOM or hit 413s. Use presigned URLs (S3/R2) for direct-to-storage uploads, and validate MIME/size on the server when you presign (client accept is bypassable). For >100 MB or flaky networks, use Uppy + tus resumable uploads. Always enforce content-type and re-check on the storage side.

Real usage — Zustand store with selectors

import { create } from "zustand";

type CartState = {
  items: { id: string; qty: number }[];
  add: (id: string) => void;
  total: () => number;
};

export const useCart = create<CartState>((set, get) => ({
  items: [],
  add: (id) =>
    set((s) => {
      const found = s.items.find((i) => i.id === id);
      return found
        ? { items: s.items.map((i) => (i.id === id ? { ...i, qty: i.qty + 1 } : i)) }
        : { items: [...s.items, { id, qty: 1 }] };
    }),
  total: () => get().items.reduce((n, i) => n + i.qty, 0),
}));

// Subscribe to a slice only — avoids re-render when unrelated state changes:
// const count = useCart((s) => s.items.length);

Senior gotcha: The #1 Zustand mistake is const state = useStore() (no selector) — it subscribes to the whole store and re-renders on every change; always pass a selector and, for object/array selections, an equality fn (useShallow) to avoid infinite render loops. In RSC, global client stores are client-only — don't read them in Server Components. For SSR (Next.js), create the store per request (via a provider/factory) instead of a module singleton, or you leak one user's state into another's render. Don't reach for global state where server state (TanStack Query) belongs — caching server data in Zustand is a common architecture smell.

Real usage — TanStack Query mutation with optimistic update

"use client";
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";

export function useToggleDone() {
  const qc = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: (id: string) => fetch(`/api/todos/${id}/toggle`, { method: "POST" }),
    onMutate: async (id) => {
      await qc.cancelQueries({ queryKey: ["todos"] });
      const prev = qc.getQueryData<Todo[]>(["todos"]);
      qc.setQueryData<Todo[]>(["todos"], (old) =>
        old?.map((t) => (t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t)),
      );
      return { prev }; // rollback context
    },
    onError: (_e, _id, ctx) => qc.setQueryData(["todos"], ctx?.prev),
    onSettled: () => qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["todos"] }),
  });
}

Senior gotcha: In Next.js App Router, don't use TanStack Query for the initial data fetch — fetch in Server Components and pass data down, or hydrate via dehydrate/HydrationBoundary; using a client query for first load defeats RSC streaming and ships a loading spinner instead of HTML. Query keys must be serializable and stable; an inline object literal as a key creates a new reference each render and misses the cache. Optimistic updates without the onError rollback leave the UI lying when the request fails.

// messages/en.json -> { "Cart": { "items": "{count, plural, =0 {Empty} one {# item} other {# items}}" } }
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";

export default function Cart({ count }: { count: number }) {
  const t = useTranslations("Cart");
  return <p>{t("items", { count })}</p>; // ICU plural, server-rendered, no client JS
}

Senior gotcha: Loading all locales' message bundles into the client is the classic i18n bundle bloat — split by route/locale (next-intl) or compile per-locale (Paraglide) so a user only downloads their language. Use ICU MessageFormat for plurals/gender, never string concatenation, or translations break grammatically. Prefer native Intl.* (NumberFormat, DateTimeFormat, RelativeTimeFormat, PluralRules) over shipping formatting libraries — they're free and built in. SSR caveat: format dates/numbers with an explicit locale and timezone, or server and client disagree and hydration warns.

Real usage — Expo Router screen + Reanimated

// app/profile/[id].tsx — Expo Router file-based route
import { View, Text, Pressable } from "react-native";
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import Animated, { useSharedValue, withSpring, useAnimatedStyle } from "react-native-reanimated";

export default function Profile() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
  const scale = useSharedValue(1);
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({ transform: [{ scale: scale.value }] }));

  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" }}>
      <Pressable
        onPressIn={() => (scale.value = withSpring(0.92))}
        onPressOut={() => (scale.value = withSpring(1))}
      >
        <Animated.View style={[{ padding: 24, backgroundColor: "#6366f1", borderRadius: 16 }, style]}>
          <Text style={{ color: "white" }}>User {id}</Text>
        </Animated.View>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: RN 0.76+ defaults to the New Architecture (Fabric/TurboModules) — some older native libraries aren't compatible and will crash or no-op; check New Arch support before adding a dep. Reanimated worklets run on the UI thread, so you can't touch React state or JS-thread closures inside useAnimatedStyle (use shared values). With Expo, adding native modules means you've left "Expo Go" — you need a development build (EAS) and Expo Go will silently lack the module. Test on real devices; the iOS simulator hides performance and gesture issues.

Real usage — Inngest durable function (code-first)

import { inngest } from "./client";

export const onSignup = inngest.createFunction(
  { id: "welcome-sequence" },
  { event: "user/signed_up" },
  async ({ event, step }) => {
    // each step is independently retried + memoized; the function survives restarts
    await step.run("send-welcome", () => sendEmail(event.data.email, "welcome"));
    await step.sleep("wait-1-day", "1d");
    const opened = await step.run("check-open", () => didOpen(event.data.userId));
    if (!opened) await step.run("nudge", () => sendEmail(event.data.email, "nudge"));
  },
);

Senior gotcha: Code-first durable engines (Inngest, Trigger.dev, Temporal) replay your function to rebuild state, so every step.run must be deterministic and idempotent — no Math.random()/Date.now()/direct side-effects outside a step, or replays diverge and you double-send emails. No-code iPaaS (Zapier/Make) is billed per task/operation and gets expensive fast at volume; model the cost before automating high-frequency events. Self-hosted (n8n) shifts that cost to ops + scaling responsibility.

Real usage — ElevenLabs streaming TTS (server route)

// app/api/tts/route.ts — stream audio so playback starts before full synthesis
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { text } = await req.json();
  const upstream = await fetch(
    "https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/VOICE_ID/stream",
    {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "xi-api-key": process.env.ELEVENLABS_KEY!, "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ text, model_id: "eleven_turbo_v2_5" }),
    },
  );
  return new Response(upstream.body, { headers: { "content-type": "audio/mpeg" } });
}

Senior gotcha: Keep STT/TTS keys server-side and proxy/stream through your backend — exposing an ElevenLabs/Deepgram key in the client lets anyone burn your quota. Stream audio (chunked) so playback starts immediately instead of waiting for full synthesis. Voice cloning needs explicit consent and carries legal/ethical exposure. Browser autoplay rules mean generated audio still needs a user gesture to play.

Real usage — Next.js dynamic OG image (satori under the hood)

// app/blog/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx
import { ImageResponse } from "next/og";

export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 };
export const contentType = "image/png";

export default async function Og({ params }: { params: { slug: string } }) {
  const post = await getPost(params.slug);
  return new ImageResponse(
    (
      <div style={{ display: "flex", width: "100%", height: "100%",
                    alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center",
                    background: "#0f172a", color: "white", fontSize: 64 }}>
        {post.title}
      </div>
    ),
    size,
  );
}

Senior gotcha: satori supports a limited CSS subset — display: flex is required on every multi-child element (no block/grid), no external CSS, and custom fonts must be fetched and passed as buffers (it can't read your bundled font automatically). Generation runs per-request on the edge, so cache the image (immutable URL keyed by content) or you pay render cost on every crawler hit. Test the actual PNG — what renders in a browser won't match satori's engine.

Real usage — tsup config for publishing a library

// tsup.config.ts — emit ESM + CJS + types, tree-shakeable
import { defineConfig } from "tsup";

export default defineConfig({
  entry: ["src/index.ts"],
  format: ["esm", "cjs"],
  dts: true,        // generate .d.ts
  sourcemap: true,
  clean: true,
  treeshake: true,

Real usage — Next.js Server Component + Server Action

// app/notes/page.tsx — runs on the server, no client JS for the list
import { db } from "@/lib/db";
import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache";

async function addNote(formData: FormData) {
  "use server";
  await db.note.create({ data: { text: String(formData.get("text")) } });
  revalidatePath("/notes"); // re-render the server component with fresh data
}

export default async function NotesPage() {
  const notes = await db.note.findMany();
  return (
    <main>
      <form action={addNote} className="flex gap-2">
        <input name="text" className="rounded border px-2" />
        <button className="rounded bg-black px-3 py-1 text-white">Add</button>
      </form>
      <ul>{notes.map((n) => <li key={n.id}>{n.text}</li>)}</ul>
    </main>
  );
}

Senior gotcha: Server Actions are public POST endpoints — they look like local function calls but run on the server and accept arbitrary input; always authenticate + validate (Zod) inside the action, never trust the closure. Don't import server-only code (DB, secrets) into Client Components — use import "server-only" to fail the build if you do. revalidatePath/revalidateTag are how you refresh RSC data; forgetting them leaves stale UI after mutations. Avoid Astro/Qwik for highly interactive app shells — their strengths are content sites; a complex dashboard fits Next/React Router better.

  • axe-core / Pa11y — a11y.
  • Lighthouse CI — perf budgets.
  • k6 / Artillery / Locust — load testing.
  • Maestro — mobile E2E.
  • Detox — RN E2E.
  • Selenium Grid — legacy.
  • Sauce Labs / BrowserStack / LambdaTest — cloud devices.

Decision matrix

PickStrengthsWhen to pick
VitestVite-native, fast, Jest-compatible API, ESM-firstDefault unit/component tests
PlaywrightMulti-browser, auto-wait, trace viewer, parallelDefault E2E
StorybookComponent isolation, a11y/test addons, docsComponent dev + visual baseline
Testing LibraryUser-centric queries, accessible-by-defaultComponent tests (with Vitest/Jest)
axe-core + PlaywrightAutomated a11y in CICatch a11y regressions
Lost Pixel / ChromaticVisual regressionCatch unintended UI diffs

Real usage — Playwright E2E with auto-waiting + accessible locators

import { test, expect } from "@playwright/test";

test("user can sign in", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/login");
  await page.getByLabel("Email").fill("ada@example.com");        // by accessible label
  await page.getByLabel("Password").fill("hunter2hunter2");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in" }).click();   // by role
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Dashboard" })).toBeVisible(); // auto-waits
});

Senior gotcha: Use role/label locators (getByRole, getByLabel), not CSS/XPath — they're resilient to refactors and double as a11y assertions; brittle selectors are the #1 source of flaky E2E. Don't add manual waitForTimeout sleeps; rely on Playwright's auto-waiting/web-first assertions. Test the production build in E2E (dev has different bundling/HMR behavior). Visual-regression tools need deterministic rendering — freeze time/animations/fonts or you get false diffs.

Part 28 — Engineering analytics + productivity

  • LinearB — DORA metrics + engineering ops.
  • Swarmia — engineering analytics + retros.
  • Jellyfish — engineering insights.
  • Code Climate Velocity — engineering analytics.
  • Pluralsight Flow (LinearB) — flow metrics.
  • Sleuth — DORA + deployment tracking.
  • Graphite — stacked PRs + AI review.
  • Aviator — merge queue + GitHub automation.
  • Trunk.io — code health monorepo (lint + format + check).
  • Mergify — PR automation + queue.

Decision matrix

PickStrengthsWhen to pick
Swarmia / LinearBDORA metrics, team-level insights, healthy framingEng leadership wanting flow visibility
SleuthDeployment tracking + DORAConnecting deploys to metrics
GraphiteStacked PRs + review + mergeTeams adopting stacked diffs
Aviator / MergifyMerge queues, batch CIHigh-PR-volume repos with flaky merges
Trunk.ioUnified lint/format/CI hygieneMonorepo code-health standardization

Senior gotcha: Engineering metrics are for spotting systemic bottlenecks, not ranking individuals — Goodhart's law guarantees that "PRs merged" or "lines of code" as individual KPIs get gamed and destroy trust. Use DORA at the team/system level. Merge queues prevent broken-main from semantic conflicts (two green PRs that conflict when combined) but add latency; tune batch size. Don't let dashboards substitute for talking to engineers about blockers.

Part 29 — Domain-specific platforms

29.1 Real estate / maps / location

  • Carto — geospatial analytics + maps.
  • Foursquare API — POI data.
  • What3Words — 3-word location addressing.

Senior gotcha: Map tiles and geocoding are metered and pricey at scale (Google Maps, Mapbox) — cache geocoding results, debounce autocomplete, and consider OSS tiles (MapLibre + self-hosted/Protomaps) to escape per-load fees. Never expose a map API key without HTTP-referer / key restrictions, or it gets scraped and billed to you. Large geo overlays belong on WebGL (deck.gl), not DOM markers.

29.2 Music / media

  • Spotify Web API — playback, playlists.
  • SoundCloud / Apple Music APIs.
  • YouTube Data API + Player.

Senior gotcha: Music/video APIs gate playback behind OAuth + active-subscription checks and restrictive ToS — the Spotify Web Playback SDK requires Premium and can't be used to build a competing player; read the terms. YouTube Data API has a tight daily quota; cache and batch. Keep OAuth tokens server-side and refresh them; never ship client secrets.

29.3 Health / fitness

  • Apple HealthKit Web / Google Fit APIs.
  • Fitbit API.
  • Garmin Connect IQ.

Senior gotcha: Health data is regulated PII (HIPAA in the US, GDPR special-category in the EU) — minimize what you store, encrypt at rest and in transit, and get explicit consent. HealthKit is on-device (no true web API; you need a native/Capacitor bridge). OAuth scopes should be least-privilege; users will (rightly) deny broad health-data requests.

29.4 Travel / hospitality

  • Amadeus / Sabre — flights, hotels.
  • Booking.com Affiliate APIs.
  • Skyscanner Travel API.

Senior gotcha: Travel GDS APIs (Amadeus/Sabre) are complex, stateful, and rate-limited, with prices/availability that change between search and book — never cache fares as bookable; re-price at checkout. Time zones, currencies, and IATA codes are constant footguns; store everything in UTC + ISO currency and format at the edge. Expect long-tail error handling (sold-out, schedule change).

29.5 Government / civic

  • USAJOBS, OpenData APIs.
  • Stripe Tax for VAT/sales tax.
  • TaxJar / Avalara for tax.

Senior gotcha: Don't compute sales tax/VAT yourself — rates, nexus rules, and exemptions change constantly per jurisdiction; use Stripe Tax/Avalara/TaxJar as the source of truth and store their calculation for audit. Government/open-data APIs are often slow, unversioned, and rate-limited — cache aggressively and degrade gracefully when they're down.

29.6 Healthcare / HIPAA

  • AWS BAA-eligible services.
  • GCP HIPAA-compliant services.
  • Twilio HIPAA edition.
  • Notion / Slack do NOT support HIPAA (commercial tiers).

Senior gotcha: HIPAA requires a signed BAA with every vendor that touches PHI — and only specific service tiers are BAA-eligible (standard Notion/Slack/most analytics are not; sending PHI there is a violation). Architect so PHI never flows into non-eligible tools (no PHI in logs, error trackers, or client analytics). Encrypt, audit-log access, and minimize the PHI surface.

29.7 Web3 / crypto (if relevant)

  • Wagmi + viem — typed Web3 React hooks.
  • RainbowKit / ConnectKit / Privy / Dynamic — wallet connect.
  • Alchemy / QuickNode / Infura — RPC providers.
  • thirdweb — drop-in Web3 SDK.
  • Sign-in with Ethereum (SIWE) — SIWE.io.

Real usage — wagmi + viem read a balance

"use client";
import { useAccount, useBalance } from "wagmi";

export function Balance() {
  const { address, isConnected } = useAccount();
  const { data, isLoading } = useBalance({ address });
  if (!isConnected) return <p>Connect wallet</p>;
  if (isLoading) return <p>Loading…</p>;
  return <p>{data?.formatted} {data?.symbol}</p>;
}

Senior gotcha: Treat the wallet/chain as fully untrusted client input — verify signatures and transactions server-side (SIWE for auth: verify the signed nonce on the server, don't trust the client's claimed address). Never put a private key or paid RPC key in the client; proxy RPC through your backend with rate limits. Handle chain switching, rejected transactions, and reorgs explicitly; on-chain reads can be stale or lie if you trust a single RPC.

Part 30 — High-impact widget libraries

30.1 Notifications + toasts

  • sonner (Vercel) — recommended.
  • react-hot-toast — popular.
  • react-toastify — feature-rich.
  • notistack — Material-style.

Decision matrix

PickStrengthsWhen to pick
sonnerBeautiful defaults, promise toasts, accessibleDefault 2026 toast
react-hot-toastTiny, simple APIMinimal toast needs
notistackMaterial-styled, stackingMUI apps

Senior gotcha: Mount the <Toaster /> once at the root; per-page mounts duplicate toasts. Toasts must be announced to screen readers (aria-live) — sonner handles this; a custom div does not. Don't put critical/blocking info in an auto-dismissing toast (users miss it); use a dialog/inline error for must-acknowledge states.

30.2 Skeletons + loaders

  • react-loading-skeleton — common.
  • react-content-loader — SVG-based.
  • @nextui-org/spinner — NextUI loaders.

Senior gotcha: Skeletons should match the final layout's dimensions or they cause layout shift (CLS) when content swaps in — reserve the exact height/width. In App Router, prefer loading.tsx + Suspense streaming over client-side skeleton state; you get HTML-level loading UI for free. Don't show a spinner for sub-300ms loads — it flickers; delay it.

30.3 Image lazy / progressive

  • next/image — Next.js.
  • react-lazy-load-image-component.
  • blurhash — placeholder algo.
  • Plaiceholder — generate placeholders at build.

Real usage — next/image with blur placeholder

import Image from "next/image";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <Image
      src="/hero.jpg"
      alt="Product dashboard"
      width={1200}
      height={630}
      placeholder="blur"
      priority           // above-the-fold LCP image: preload, don't lazy-load
      sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 1200px"
    />
  );
}

Senior gotcha: Set priority on the LCP image (hero) so it isn't lazy-loaded — lazy-loading your largest contentful paint tanks Core Web Vitals. Always give width/height (or fill + sized parent) to reserve space and avoid CLS. next/image optimizes on-demand; for many images, configure a CDN loader or you bottleneck on the optimizer. Generate blur placeholders at build time (Plaiceholder) for static images.

30.4 Carousels (covered, recap)

  • Embla, Keen Slider, Swiper.

Senior gotcha (recap): Embla is the lean default; reach for Swiper only when you need its heavy feature modules, and tree-shake them. All carousels need keyboard support and a pause control for autoplay (WCAG). Set slide sizing in CSS to prevent first-paint layout shift before hydration.

30.5 Drag-drop (covered, recap)

  • dnd-kit, @hello-pangea/dnd, React Aria DnD.

Senior gotcha (recap): dnd-kit is the modern default; react-beautiful-dnd is archived (use @hello-pangea/dnd). Provide stable unique IDs and keyboard + screen-reader support — pointer-only DnD is an a11y failure.

30.6 Date pickers

  • react-aria DatePicker.
  • react-day-picker.
  • react-datepicker (legacy popular).
  • MUI DatePicker.

Senior gotcha: Date pickers are the timezone/SSR hotspot — compute "today" client-side or pass an explicit zone, and parse with @internationalized/date/Temporal rather than raw new Date(string) (which interprets ambiguous strings differently per engine). react-aria's DatePicker has the strongest a11y + i18n; prefer it where the bar is high.

30.7 Code highlighting

  • Shiki — most accurate (uses VS Code grammars).
  • Prism.js — small + popular.
  • Highlight.js — automatic detection.
  • rehype-pretty-code — MDX + Shiki integration.

Real usage — Shiki at build time (zero client JS)

import { codeToHtml } from "shiki";

// Run on the server / at build (RSC or generateStaticParams), ship plain HTML:
const html = await codeToHtml(source, { lang: "tsx", theme: "github-dark" });
// <pre> with inline styles — no highlighter ships to the browser

Senior gotcha: Run Shiki on the server / at build (it's accurate but heavy — bundles VS Code grammars + themes); shipping it to the client adds hundreds of KB. For MDX, use rehype-pretty-code so highlighting happens at build. If you must highlight client-side dynamic code, Prism/Highlight.js are lighter but less accurate. Don't dangerouslySetInnerHTML untrusted code without sanitizing.

30.8 Markdown

  • react-markdown — render MD.
  • MDX (mdx-js) — MD + components.
  • @uiw/react-md-editor — editor.
  • marked / remark / rehype — parsers.
  • unified ecosystem — pluggable.

Real usage — react-markdown with GFM, safe by default

import ReactMarkdown from "react-markdown";
import remarkGfm from "remark-gfm";

export function Markdown({ source }: { source: string }) {
  // react-markdown does NOT use dangerouslySetInnerHTML — safe against HTML injection by default
  return <ReactMarkdown remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}>{source}</ReactMarkdown>;
}

Senior gotcha: react-markdown is XSS-safe by default because it builds a React tree (no raw HTML) — but the moment you add rehype-raw to allow embedded HTML, you must add rehype-sanitize, or user content becomes a stored-XSS vector. MDX executes code/components, so never render untrusted MDX (it's effectively eval). For user-generated content, prefer plain Markdown + sanitization over MDX.

30.9 Search UI

  • Algolia InstantSearch.
  • Typesense InstantSearch adapter.
  • Meilisearch instant-meilisearch.
  • cmdk / kbar — command palette.

Decision matrix

PickStrengthsWhen to pick
Algolia InstantSearchHosted, fast, polished widgets, typo toleranceDon't want to run search infra
Typesense / MeilisearchOSS, self-hostable, InstantSearch adaptersOwn your search, cost control
cmdk / kbarIn-app command palette (Cmd-K)Navigation/actions, not full-text search

Senior gotcha: Use search-only (public) API keys scoped to specific indices on the client — never the admin key, which can wipe your index. Build the index server-side and keep secrets there. Debounce queries and respect the provider's rate/usage limits. For self-hosted (Typesense/Meilisearch), the search server is internet-facing; lock it behind your API, don't expose it directly.

30.10 Charts (recap)

  • Recharts default; ECharts large data; Tremor dashboards.

Senior gotcha (recap): Recharts (SVG) is the easy default under a few thousand points; switch to ECharts/uPlot (canvas) for large or live data. Give responsive charts an explicit height to avoid SSR 0×0 + CLS, and disable animation on dashboards that re-render on polling.

Appendix — Stack picking shortcuts

A. Build a new SaaS in 2026 (modern default)

  • Next.js 15 App Router + RSC + Server Actions.
  • shadcn/ui + Tailwind v4.
  • TanStack Query + Zustand.
  • Zod + React Hook Form.
  • Drizzle ORM + Neon Postgres.
  • Better-Auth (or Clerk if you can pay).
  • Resend + React Email.
  • PostHog (analytics + flags + replay).
  • Sentry (errors + perf).
  • Stripe (payments).
  • Vercel (hosting) or Cloudflare Pages (cheaper at scale).

Why these fit together: RSC fetches data server-side (no client query for first load) → TanStack Query handles client-side mutations/refetch → Zustand only for true UI state → one Zod schema validates RHF on the client and the Server Action on the server → Drizzle gives typed queries with Neon's serverless HTTP driver (no pool exhaustion). The whole stack is zero-runtime-CSS (Tailwind) and RSC-safe.

B. Build an indie SaaS on free tiers

  • Vercel free + Cloudflare R2 + Neon free + Resend free.
  • PostHog Cloud free + Sentry free.
  • Better Stack free uptime + Atlassian Statuspage free.
  • Stripe (no monthly fee; just transaction %)

Watch the free-tier cliffs: Neon free scales to zero (cold starts), Vercel free has function/bandwidth caps, Resend free caps daily sends. Architect to degrade, and know each tier's hard limit before launch-day traffic hits it.

C. Build a collab editor (Figma-like)

  • Cloudflare Pages + Workers + Durable Objects.
  • R2 storage + D1 / Turso for metadata.
  • Yjs + Liveblocks OR self-host Hocuspocus.
  • Tiptap or Lexical (rich text).
  • Tldraw or custom WebGL for canvas.
  • WorkOS for enterprise SSO.

The hard part is sync, not UI: Yjs (CRDT) handles conflict-free merges; Durable Objects give one authoritative coordinator per document (ideal for presence + persistence). Store the Yjs doc as the source of truth, snapshot to R2. Tiptap binds to Yjs directly for collaborative rich text.

D. Build an AI SaaS

  • Next.js + Vercel Edge runtime.
  • Vercel AI SDK with OpenRouter / AI Gateway.
  • Pinecone / Turbopuffer for vectors.
  • Langfuse for LLM observability.
  • Helicone for caching + cost control.
  • Braintrust / LangSmith for evals.

Stream and observe: Use the AI SDK's streaming (streamText → useChat) so tokens render as they arrive; route through a gateway (OpenRouter/Helicone) for fallback + cost caps + caching; log every call to Langfuse and gate prompt changes behind evals (Braintrust). Keep model keys server-side; never call providers from the browser.

E. Build a marketing + blog site

  • Astro + Tailwind.
  • Sanity / Contentful CMS (or local MDX).
  • Cloudflare Pages.
  • Plausible / Fathom (privacy analytics).
  • FormSpark / Formspree for forms.
  • Resend for newsletter.

Ship ~0 JS: Astro's island architecture renders content as static HTML and only hydrates interactive islands — ideal for LCP/SEO. Use MDX for authored content, a headless CMS only if non-devs publish. Privacy analytics (Plausible/Fathom) avoid cookie banners.

End of Volume II. Pair Doc 11 (services) + Doc 12 (libs/AI/design) for the full tools panorama. Together you have a reference of 450+ tools senior FE engineers use in real production.

Treat them as marketing-page-only — lazy-load with next/dynamic({ ssr: false }) , and never ship them in the authenticated app bundle. Also audit licenses: "copy-paste" kits often relicense MIT components you could get free; pay for the design, not the code. 1.4 Senior gotchas Component libs bloat fast — measure the bundle impact of every import. shadcn (copy-paste) > npm component lib if you need to customize heavily. Lock dark mode + theming early; refactor later is painful. Accessibility regressions are easy when restyling; test with axe before shipping. Expanded checklist Measure, don't guess. Wire @next/bundle-analyzer or vite-bundle-visualizer into CI and fail PRs that grow the entry chunk past a budget. Any interactive primitive is a client component; keep them as leaves and pass server data as props. A stray "use client" at the top of a layout poisons the whole subtree. Theme tokens once. Run axe-core via Playwright on key flows; restyling a focus ring or removing an outline silently regresses keyboard users. Hydration safety. Anything reading window , localStorage , or Date.now() at render must be gated to useEffect or ssr: false , or you get the dreaded text-content-mismatch.
